input.content:
> **TL;DR** — Your conversation with the Studio is the product, and right now it evaporates the moment you reload the page. Everything else about you — your settings, your brief, your notifications — lives in your browser's `localStorage`, so two browsers have two different you, and a desktop app and a web tab disagree. After this issue the conversation and what the agent learned live in the same event-sourced ODI store everything else already uses, so you can close the app, come back tomorrow on another device, and pick the thread up exactly where you left it — and the agent remembers what it learned.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Area** | `area/studio`, `area/core` |
| **Priority** | `priority/high` |
| **Kind** | specification |
| **Depends on** | {{ISSUE_01}} |
| **Related PRs** | #71, #43 |
| **Blocks** | {{ISSUE_05}} (the audit trail needs the same substrate) |

---

## The problem

An AI-native product is one where the *thread* is the durable artifact. This one throws the thread away.

**1. The transcript is React state and nothing else.**
`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:279` — `const [messages, setMessages] = useState<ChatMessage[]>([])`. `clearChat` at `:830-838` wipes it. A page reload destroys it. There is no persistence call anywhere in the file.

**2. Everything else is `localStorage`, so "you" is per-browser.**
`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:51-56` — the storage keys are:

| Key | Holds | Line |
|---|---|---|
| `studio.settings` | LLM base URL, api key, model, mcp url | `:435-442` |
| `studio.brief` | the onboarding brief (product, url, target user, job, problem) | `:453-462` |
| `studio.displayName` | display name | `:270` |
| `studio.canvas` | a canvas **cache** | `:515-531` |
| `studio.notifications` | the notification feed | `:292-299` (→ {{ISSUE_02}}) |
| `studio.setupDraft` | the setup conversation draft | `components/setup/SetupConversation.tsx:27-28` |
| `studio.onboarding` | onboarding state | `onboarding/storage.ts:14` |

The domain store — `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/sqlite_repository.py` — is event-sourced, shared by the CLI, the MCP server, and the sidecar, and holds none of this. The **api key** and the **brief** are among the things that live only in one browser.

**3. The agent has no memory at all.**
There is no `remember` tool. There is no `memory` SSE event. The local tool set is exactly `{render_ui, add_connector}` (`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:210-212`). The brief is injected into the system prompt as a block of text (`chat.py:41-61`) and can only be changed through the setup conversation — the agent cannot update it, correct it, or learn anything new.

**4. The brief is a second, competing source of truth.**
`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/schemas.py` — `StudioBrief` is a request-scoped object, not a stored entity. Two sessions disagree. The CLI cannot see it. The MCP server cannot see it.

**5. The event store already has the right shape, and it is half-used.**
`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/intent_store.py:70-267` — an append-only `events` table with `event_id`, `workspace_id`, `device_id`, `timestamp`, `event_type`, `payload`, `server_seq`, plus a `sync_state` table. The sync half (`insert_remote`, `mark_synced`, `retag_workspace`, `max_server_seq`, `get_cursor`, `set_cursor`, `pending_count`) has **zero callers** anywhere in the repository. `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/events.py:49-99` — the `EventStore` protocol's sync half and `resolve_device_id`/`default_device_path` are likewise unused. `SQLiteRepository.reload()` (`sqlite_repository.py:400-402`) is never called.

So the substrate for durable, portable, multi-device memory **already exists and is unclaimed**.

**6. `device_id` is not actually a device.**
`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/sqlite_repository.py:31` reads `AGENTIC_ODI_DEVICE_ID` and otherwise hardcodes `"local"`. Every install writes the same device id.

## What a person experiences

A person has a long afternoon session with the Studio about the job their customers are trying to get done. They close the laptop. The next morning, on a different machine, they open the Studio. The conversation is there — the whole thread, with every card they were shown, in order. The agent greets them with what it learned: *"Last time we were working on secrets rotation for platform engineers. You told me the approval step is what hurts."* They can see a **"What I've learned"** panel listing the observations the agent wrote down, and they can confirm, edit, or dismiss any of them. If the agent learns something wrong, they correct it and it is corrected everywhere, not just in that browser.

## Specification

### 4.1 New domain entities

Add to `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py`:

```python
class Conversation(BaseModel):
    id: str
    title: str | None = None          # derived from the first user turn
    created_at: datetime
    updated_at: datetime
    workspace_id: str = "local"
    device_id: str = "local"
    archived: bool = False

class Message(BaseModel):
    id: str
    conversation_id: str
    role: Literal["user", "assistant", "tool", "system"]
    content: str
    parts: list[dict] = []            # ordered parts: prose, ui specs, tool events
    tool_calls: list[dict] = []
    created_at: datetime
    model: str | None = None
    tokens_in: int | None = None
    tokens_out: int | None = None

class Observation(BaseModel):
    id: str
    conversation_id: str | None = None
    text: str
    category: Literal["career", "opportunity", "business", "customer", "constraint", "decision", "other"] = "other"
    status: Literal["proposed", "confirmed", "dismissed"] = "proposed"
    source_message_id: str | None = None
    created_at: datetime
    updated_at: datetime
```

`Observation` is the "memory" primitive: a short, attributable fact the agent believes, which a person can confirm, edit, or dismiss.

### 4.2 Persistence

- Extend the `Repository` protocol, `InMemoryRepository`, and `SQLiteRepository` with:
  - `add_conversation`, `get_conversation`, `list_conversations`, `update_conversation`, `delete_conversation`
  - `add_message`, `get_message`, `list_messages(conversation_id, limit, before)`
  - `add_observation`, `get_observation`, `list_observations(status)`, `update_observation`
- Event types `CONVERSATION_CREATED`, `CONVERSATION_UPDATED`, `MESSAGE_APPENDED`, `OBSERVATION_CREATED`, `OBSERVATION_UPDATED` in `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/sqlite_repository.py:51-112`.
- New tables `conversations`, `messages`, `observations` in the schema at `sqlite_repository.py:18-37`.
- **The `parts` payload is the ordered list the SPA renders.** It must round-trip exactly, so a reloaded conversation is pixel-identical to the one that was live — including every `ui` spec that was rendered. Store the raw spec; re-validate it on read with the same client-side validator (`apps/studio/src/ui/protocol.ts`) so a stored spec from an older catalog version degrades to the `unsupported` fallback rather than crashing.

### 4.3 The `remember` tool

Add a third local tool to the studio agent loop, alongside `render_ui` and `add_connector`.

- `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:141-212` — the local-tool dispatch. Add `remember`:
  - **Arguments**: `text` (required, ≤ 300 chars), `category` (optional, one of the `Observation` categories).
  - **Behaviour**: writes an `Observation` with `status="proposed"`, emits a `memory` SSE event, and returns a short confirmation string to the model.
  - The tool must be **advisory**: the agent cannot confirm its own memory. A person confirms.
- Emit a `memory` SSE event: `{observation_id, text, category, status, created_at}`.
- Update `apps/studio/src/api/sse.ts:10-46` — the parser must handle the new event name.
- `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:717-782` — handle the event: append to the observations list, show a toast with **Confirm** / **Dismiss** actions.

### 4.4 System prompt

`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:28-38` — add two rules to `SYSTEM_PROMPT`:

```
9. Remember: when the PM states a fact about their product, customer, business, or
   constraint that will still matter later, call `remember` once with that fact in
   their words. Never remember a score, a name you inferred, or anything the PM did
   not say. Never write an observation you would not defend out loud.
10. The brief and the confirmed observations are the only context you carry forward.
    If a fact is missing, ask — do not assume, and do not invent history.
```

Also append the **confirmed** observations to the prompt as a context block, alongside the existing brief block (`chat.py:41-61`, `_brief_block`). Confirmed only — a proposed observation is not yet true.

### 4.5 API surface

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/conversations?limit=20` | List conversations, newest first |
| `POST` | `/api/conversations` | Create |
| `GET` | `/api/conversations/{id}` | Get one, with its messages |
| `PATCH` | `/api/conversations/{id}` | Rename / archive |
| `DELETE` | `/api/conversations/{id}` | Delete (cascade to messages) |
| `GET` | `/api/conversations/{id}/messages?limit=200` | Ordered message list |
| `POST` | `/api/conversations/{id}/messages` | Append a message (used by the SPA to persist user turns) |
| `GET` | `/api/observations?status=proposed` | List observations |
| `PATCH` | `/api/observations/{id}` | Confirm / dismiss / edit |

Both backends, per `router.py:51-52`. The sidecar must also own the SSE `memory` event.

### 4.6 MCP tools

Add to `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py` and to `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py`:

- `list_conversations(limit: int = 20)`
- `get_conversation(conversation_id: str, message_limit: int = 200)`
- `list_observations(status: str | None = None)`
- `confirm_observation(observation_id: str)`
- `dismiss_observation(observation_id: str)`

This is what makes memory available to **any** agent that talks to the MCP server — not only the Studio's own loop.

### 4.7 Front end

**Conversation persistence** — `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx`:

- On boot, if `localStorage` has no `studio.conversationId`, create one via `POST /api/conversations` and store the id. If it has one, fetch it and **restore the transcript**.
- On every message, append it to the conversation: the user turn immediately; the assistant turn when the `message` SSE event arrives (with its `parts`).
- On `clearChat` (`:830-838`), **archive** the current conversation and start a new one. Do not delete history. Deleting must be an explicit, confirmed action in a conversation list.
- Add a **conversation switcher**: a small affordance in `apps/studio/src/components/layout/StudioBar.tsx` listing recent conversations by title and time. Clicking one loads it.
- **The transcript must survive a reload and a crash.** A test that reloads the page and asserts the thread is intact is mandatory.

**The "What I've learned" panel** — new component `apps/studio/src/components/workspace/MemoryPanel.tsx`, surfaced in the workspace rail (`apps/studio/src/components/workspace/WorkbenchRail.tsx`):

- lists observations newest first, grouped by `status`;
- each row shows the text, the category, and the source message excerpt;
- actions: **Confirm**, **Edit**, **Dismiss**;
- confirmed observations are visually distinct;
- there is a **"Forget"** action on confirmed observations that removes the observation from the prompt block entirely.

**Migration of the brief** — `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:453-462`:

- The brief stays in `localStorage` for now, but the sidecar must be able to read it. Add `GET /api/brief` and `PUT /api/brief` backed by a `Brief` entity in the store (persisted like everything else). The SPA syncs on boot and on change; `localStorage` becomes a cache, not the source of truth.
- `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/schemas.py` — `StudioBrief` becomes a stored entity with a stable id.

**Settings** — `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:435-442`: the **API key must not live in `localStorage`**. Move it to the sidecar: `POST /api/settings` stores it in the sidecar's own config file (`~/.config/agentic-odi/`), and the SPA reads a redacted version (`{"has_api_key": true, "masked": "sk-…4f2a"}`). The SPA never receives the secret back. See {{ISSUE_13}} for the wider security posture.

### 4.8 Multi-device, honestly

- `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/events.py:73-99` — `resolve_device_id` and `default_device_path` exist and are unused. **Use them.** Replace the hardcoded `"local"` at `sqlite_repository.py:31` with a real, persisted device id: `~/.config/agentic-odi/device-id` (created once, mode `0600`).
- Add `workspace_id` to every conversation, message, and observation. It defaults to the `AGENTIC_ODI_WORKSPACE` env var, defaulting to `local` (matching `sqlite_repository.py:29`).
- **Do not implement sync.** The `sync_state` table and the unused sync half of `EventStore` are explicitly deferred. This issue makes the data *durable and portable in format*; a later issue may make it sync. Do not half-implement a sync protocol.

## Non-negotiable constraints

- **Nothing the person said is lost.** A reload must restore the exact thread.
- **The agent never confirms its own memory.** Only a person can confirm or dismiss an observation.
- **A dismissed observation is never injected into a prompt again.** Not in this session, not in the next.
- The API key must never be written to `localStorage` or returned to the SPA in plain text.
- Do not implement cloud sync of conversations in this issue.
- The event-sourced substrate stays the substrate: new state goes through `IntentStore`, not through ad-hoc tables.
- The sidecar must not contact the LLM to store or retrieve a conversation.

## Out of scope

- Cloud sync of conversations between devices → explicitly deferred.
- A semantic search over history.
- A "What I've learned" panel in the CLI → the MCP tools make it possible, but the CLI UI is a later issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Conversation`, `Message`, and `Observation` exist in `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py` and are exported from `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/__init__.py`.
- [ ] `Repository`, `InMemoryRepository`, and `SQLiteRepository` all persist conversations, messages, and observations; the SQLite implementation is event-sourced and survives a reload.
- [ ] `Message.parts` round-trips exactly, including `ui` specs, and a stored spec that fails the current client validator degrades to the `unsupported` fallback rather than throwing.
- [ ] A `remember` local tool exists in the studio agent loop and emits a `memory` SSE event.
- [ ] `apps/studio/src/api/sse.ts` parses the `memory` event.
- [ ] The system prompt tells the agent when to remember and forbids it from writing an observation it would not defend; confirmed observations are injected into the prompt and proposed ones are not.
- [ ] `GET/POST /api/conversations`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/conversations/{id}`, `GET/POST /api/conversations/{id}/messages`, `GET/PATCH /api/observations` exist and work under both backends.
- [ ] `list_conversations`, `get_conversation`, `list_observations`, `confirm_observation`, `dismiss_observation` exist as MCP tools and are registered in `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py`.
- [ ] Reloading the page restores the exact transcript, including rendered surfaces, in order.
- [ ] `clearChat` archives rather than deletes; deleting requires explicit confirmation.
- [ ] A conversation switcher exists and lists recent conversations.
- [ ] A "What I've learned" panel exists with Confirm / Edit / Dismiss, and "Forget" removes a confirmed observation from future prompts.
- [ ] The API key is stored server-side and the SPA receives only a redacted form.
- [ ] `device_id` is a real persisted id, not the hardcoded `"local"`.
- [ ] No sync protocol is half-implemented.

## Verification

```bash

uv run --directory apps/mcp-server pytest
uv run --directory apps/studio-api pytest
npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run
npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck && npm --prefix apps/studio run lint
uv run --directory packages/core mypy .
uv run --directory apps/studio-api mypy .
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .
```

Add tests:

- `packages/core/tests/test_conversations.py` — create, append, list, archive, delete-cascade.
- `packages/core/tests/test_observations.py` — propose, confirm, dismiss; a dismissed observation is excluded from the prompt block.
- `packages/core/tests/test_sqlite_repository.py` — conversations, messages, and observations survive a reload; `parts` round-trip.
- `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_conversation.py` — the routes under both backends; the `memory` SSE event is emitted when the model calls `remember`.
- `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.test.tsx` (new) — **reload restores the transcript**; a `memory` event creates a toast; a `remember` tool call is persisted.

input.content:
> **TL;DR** — Today the agent can only say things back to you. Every button it draws is a sentence typed into the chat, and every tool it calls happens immediately and invisibly — there is no way to approve a thing before it happens, no way to say "not that one", and no record of what the agent actually did on your data. After this issue the agent can **propose an action, wait for your yes or no, adjust it, and leave a receipt.** You stay in the loop; the loop is designed, not accidental.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Area** | `area/studio`, `area/core` |
| **Priority** | `priority/high` |
| **Kind** | specification |
| **Depends on** | {{ISSUE_04}} (the same store and the same audit substrate) |
| **Related PRs** | #62, #70 |
| **Blocks** | {{ISSUE_18}} (background agents must not act without a mandate) |

---

## The problem

The product's stated premise is *"you express intent, and you get signals"* — the agent does the work. But the current design gives the agent exactly one way to influence the world: it calls MCP tools, immediately, and the result is a string.

**1. There is no approval concept anywhere.**
A full read of `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:235-373` shows the loop: list tools → call the LLM → execute every tool call it asks for → feed the result back → repeat up to `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 3`. There is no branch where the agent says "may I?" and waits.

**2. The action model is one-directional and lossy.**
`apps/studio/src/ui/actions.ts:8-12`:

```ts
export interface UiAction {
  label: string;
  intent: string;        // ← the entire action model
  tone: "primary" | "ghost";
}
```

Every button in every card is a **string sent to the model as the next user message** (`apps/studio/src/ui/primitives.tsx:21-42` → `dispatcher.onIntent(action.intent)` → `sendMessage(intent)`). Consequences:

- You cannot approve, deny, or edit anything — you can only *say something*.
- The action's meaning is reconstructed from English by the model on every click. "Yes" and "Apply" and "Do it" are all the same action with a different label.
- There is no way to act on a suggestion **without a round trip through the chat**. The chat transcript becomes the transaction log, which makes auditing and undoing impossible.
- A card cannot carry a structured payload. `targetId` on a notification is set and never read (`apps/studio/src/types.ts:100`).

**3. Errors are swallowed into the transcript.**
`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:354-358` — an MCP exception becomes the tool result string, so the model may recover. Good. But nothing is recorded anywhere, so a person cannot see that the agent hit three failed calls and quietly gave up.

**4. There is no audit trail at all.**
The repository has no record of who asked for what. The `events` table in `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/intent_store.py:70-86` records *state changes* but not *decisions* — there is no actor, no request id, no correlation id, and no way to ask "what did the agent do while I was asleep" (which is exactly what {{ISSUE_18}} proposes to enable).

**5. The agent's identity is not modelled.**
`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:28-38` hardcodes the persona "You are Steve Jobs". There is no notion of a caller, a session, or an agent identity in any request schema. `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/schemas.py` — `ChatRequest` carries no actor.

**6. The proposed background-agent PR makes this worse.**
PR #62's `trigger_scheduled_work` (`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/services.py:391` on that branch) fabricates a success string and sets `status=COMPLETED`. If agents can act on a timer, the absence of a consent model is not a gap — it is a hazard.

## What a person experiences

The agent finds three candidate outcomes from your Gong transcripts. It does not create them. It renders a card: *"I found 3 candidate outcomes. Approve all, or open them one at a time."* Each has a checkbox, a suggested score, and a **Reason** disclosure showing the quote it came from. You approve two, edit the wording of one, and reject the third. The rejections are recorded. The agent never writes anything you did not approve.

Later, you ask the agent to *"keep an eye on the connector health and tell me if GitHub goes down."* It proposes a **standing mandate** — a small, explicit card that says exactly what it will do, how often, and what it will never do — and asks you to confirm it once. After that it acts without bothering you, and everything it does appears in a **Receipts** list you can read, filter, and export. When it does something you did not expect, the receipt is the first place you look.

## Specification

### 5.1 A proposal is a first-class thing

Add to `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py`:

```python
class ProposalKind(StrEnum):
    TOOL_CALL = "tool_call"          # run an MCP tool
    BATCH = "batch"                  # run several
    OUTCOME = "outcome"              # write a domain artifact
    MANDATE = "mandate"              # a standing permission to act later

class ProposalState(StrEnum):
    PENDING = "pending"
    APPROVED = "approved"
    DENIED = "denied"
    EDITED = "edited"
    EXECUTED = "executed"
    FAILED = "failed"
    EXPIRED = "expired"

class Proposal(BaseModel):
    id: str
    kind: ProposalKind
    title: str                       # one line, human-readable
    rationale: str                   # why the agent wants this
    tool_name: str | None = None
    tool_args: dict = {}
    payload: dict = {}               # structured payload for non-tool proposals
    state: ProposalState = ProposalState.PENDING
    requires_approval: bool = True
    expires_at: datetime | None = None
    created_at: datetime
    decided_at: datetime | None = None
    decided_by: str | None = None    # the actor, e.g. "local-user"
    execution_id: str | None = None

class Execution(BaseModel):
    id: str
    proposal_id: str | None
    actor: str                       # "agent" | "local-user" | "mandate:<id>"
    request_id: str
    tool_name: str | None
    tool_args: dict
    result_summary: str
    ok: bool
    started_at: datetime
    finished_at: datetime
    error: str | None = None
```

`Execution` is the receipt. It is the answer to *"what did the agent actually do?"*

### 5.2 The consent gate in the agent loop

`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:235-373` — restructure the tool dispatch:

1. The model calls a tool.
2. The sidecar decides whether the call needs approval, using a **policy** (below).
3. If approval is needed, the sidecar **does not execute**. It creates a `Proposal` in `PENDING`, emits a `proposal` SSE event, and tells the model: *"This action needs the PM's approval. It is now waiting as proposal <id>. Tell the PM what it would do."* The model continues and the reply explains what is pending.
4. The person approves from the UI. The sidecar executes the tool, records an `Execution`, emits an `execution` SSE event, and the transcript shows the receipt.
5. If the person denies, the sidecar records the denial, and the model is told: *"Proposal <id> was declined. Do not retry it. Continue with something else."*

**Policy** — a new module `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/consent.py`:

```python
DEFAULT_AUTO_APPROVE_TOOLS = frozenset({
    "get_jobs", "get_job", "get_job_map", "get_step", "get_outcomes",
    "get_outcome", "get_customer_outcome", "list_customer_outcomes",
    "list_evidence", "get_evidence", "compute_opportunity",
    "evaluate_outcome", "get_odi_schema", "get_odi_framework_guidelines",
    "get_capabilities",
})
```

- Read-only tools are auto-approved. The list above is derived from `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` — **derive it, do not hand-maintain it**: any tool whose name starts with `get_`/`list_`/`compute_`/`evaluate_` is read-only. The explicit set exists to pin the decision and make it testable.
- Every mutating tool (`add_*`, `update_*`, `delete_*`, `promote_*`, `add_connector`, `render_ui`? no — `render_ui` is a *view*, it is auto-approved) requires approval **by default**.
- `render_ui` is auto-approved: it renders, it does not mutate.
- The policy is configurable: `AGENTIC_ODI_AUTO_APPROVE` accepts a comma-separated tool list that is auto-approved *in addition* to the read-only set. The default is empty.
- **A standing mandate overrides the gate for the tools it names**, within its scope and expiry. Mandates are themselves proposals: creating one requires approval.

### 5.3 The approval surface

- `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` — add a `proposal` card type. It renders: title, rationale, a payload preview, and actions `approve` / `deny` / `edit` / `open`.
- `apps/studio/src/ui/actions.ts` — extend `UiAction`:

```ts
export interface UiAction {
  label: string;
  intent?: string;      // existing behavior
  kind?: "intent" | "approve" | "deny" | "edit";
  target?: string;      // proposal id
  tone?: "primary" | "ghost";
}
```

- `kind` defaults to `"intent"` when absent — **backward compatibility is required**, and {{ISSUE_03}} extends the same model. Coordinate: the two issues must agree on the final shape; the union is `{intent, approve, reject, deny, edit}`. Prefer a single shared definition; if {{ISSUE_03}} lands first, extend its `kind` union rather than introducing a second one.
- `approve` / `deny` / `edit` are dispatched **directly to the API**, not as chat text. `apps/studio/src/ui/primitives.tsx:21-42` — `ActionRow` must branch on `kind`.
- The action dispatcher lives in a new `apps/studio/src/ui/dispatcher.ts` (or is passed via the existing `UiActionContext`, `actions.ts:19-23`) and is provided by `apps/studio/src/components/chat/Conversation.tsx:142`.

### 5.4 API surface

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/proposals?state=pending` | List proposals |
| `GET` | `/api/proposals/{id}` | One proposal |
| `POST` | `/api/proposals/{id}/approve` | Approve → execute → return the `Execution` |
| `POST` | `/api/proposals/{id}/deny` | Deny |
| `POST` | `/api/proposals/{id}/edit` | Edit payload, then approve |
| `GET` | `/api/executions?limit=50` | The receipts list |
| `GET` | `/api/executions/{id}` | One receipt |

Both backends, per `router.py:51-52`.

Add to `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py` and to `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py`:

- `list_proposals(state: str | None = None)`
- `approve_proposal(proposal_id: str, edited_args: dict | None = None) -> Execution`
- `deny_proposal(proposal_id: str)`
- `list_executions(limit: int = 50)`

Note the name collision with {{ISSUE_03}}'s `approve_proposal`. **Reconcile in one place**: either {{ISSUE_03}}'s evidence proposals and this issue's action proposals share one `Proposal` entity with a `kind` discriminator, or they use distinct names (`approve_evidence_proposal` vs `approve_action_proposal`). **Preferred: one entity with a `kind` discriminator** — a person should see one list of things waiting for them, not two. Whichever lands first owns the entity; the other extends it. Document the choice in the code.

### 5.6 The audit trail

- `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/services.py` — add `ODIService.record_execution(...) -> Execution` and `ODIService.list_executions(...)`.
- Extend the `Repository` protocol, `InMemoryRepository`, and `SQLiteRepository` with `add_proposal`, `get_proposal`, `list_proposals`, `update_proposal`, `add_execution`, `list_executions`.
- Event types `PROPOSAL_CREATED`, `PROPOSAL_DECIDED`, `EXECUTION_RECORDED` in `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/sqlite_repository.py:51-112`.
- **The audit trail is append-only.** A decided proposal and a recorded execution are never updated or deleted. `deny` and `approve` append a new event; they never overwrite.
- Every `Execution` carries a `request_id`. The same `request_id` must appear in the sidecar's log line (see {{ISSUE_14}}) and in the SSE event, so a person can grep for it.

### 5.7 Mandates (standing permission)

A `MANDATE` proposal grants scoped, expiring permission:

```python
class Mandate(BaseModel):
    id: str
    name: str
    allowed_tools: list[str]
    allowed_scope: dict          # e.g. {"connector": "github"}
    max_executions: int          # default 50
    executions_used: int = 0
    expires_at: datetime
    created_at: datetime
```

- Creating a mandate requires approval.
- The sidecar checks mandates before creating a proposal for a tool call.
- A mandate that exceeds `max_executions` or `expires_at` stops applying, and the agent falls back to asking.
- Mandates are visible in Settings and revocable at any time.
- **A mandate may never authorize `delete_*` on a Job, Step, Outcome, CustomerOutcome, or the whole store.** Deletion always asks, every time. This is a hard constraint, not a default.

### 5.8 The studio's system prompt

`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:28-38` — add:

```
11. You do not have the PM's permission to change their work unless they gave it.
    When a tool call needs approval, it becomes a proposal: explain in one sentence
    what it would do and why, and let the PM decide. Never claim something was
    saved, imported, connected, or deleted unless the tool actually returned success.
```

That last clause is the anti-fabrication rule, and it is the single most important line in the prompt.

## Non-negotiable constraints

- **No mutating tool call executes without either an explicit approval or a valid mandate.**
- The audit trail is append-only.
- A denied proposal is never retried automatically.
- Every mutating MCP tool requires approval **by default**; the auto-approve list is read-only tools plus an explicit, empty, configurable override.
- Mandates never authorize destructive deletion.
- An `Execution` is recorded for **every** tool call, including auto-approved read-only ones, so the trail is complete. Read-only executions may be sampled for storage but must be countable.
- The consent gate must work when the person is not looking at the screen: an unanswered proposal stays `PENDING` and is never auto-approved by a timeout.

## Out of scope

- Background agents acting on mandates → {{ISSUE_18}} builds on this.
- A full "undo" of an executed action → the audit trail is the prerequisite; undo is a later issue.
- Delegated consent (one person approving for another) → single-user local product for now.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The agent loop creates a pending proposal instead of executing a mutating tool call.
- [ ] Approving a proposal executes it and returns an `Execution`; denying it does not execute and tells the model not to retry.
- [ ] The auto-approve set is derived from `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py`, contains only read-only tools by default, and is overridable via `AGENTIC_ODI_AUTO_APPROVE`.
- [ ] `render_ui` is auto-approved; no mutating tool is.
- [ ] A `proposal` card type exists with approve / deny / edit actions that dispatch to the API rather than to the chat.
- [ ] An action with no `kind` still behaves as `intent` (backward compatibility).
- [ ] The approval buttons have accessible names that include what is being approved, and the pending region is announced.
- [ ] `GET/POST /api/proposals`, `POST /api/proposals/{id}/approve|deny|edit`, `GET /api/executions` exist and work under both backends.
- [ ] `list_proposals`, `approve_proposal`, `deny_proposal`, `list_executions` exist as MCP tools and are registered in the contract.
- [ ] The proposal/execution entities are reconciled with {{ISSUE_03}}'s evidence proposals into one entity with a `kind` discriminator, or the divergence is documented and the names are unambiguous.
- [ ] The audit trail is append-only — decided proposals and executions are never mutated.
- [ ] Mandates are scoped, expiring, execution-capped, revocable, and never authorize destructive deletion.
- [ ] The system prompt forbids the agent from claiming an action succeeded unless the tool returned success.
- [ ] Every `Execution` carries a `request_id` that also appears in the server log line and the SSE event.

## Verification

uv run --directory apps/mcp-server pytest
uv run --directory apps/studio-api pytest
npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run
npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck && npm --prefix apps/studio run lint
uv run --directory packages/core mypy .
uv run --directory apps/studio-api mypy .
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .

input.content:
> **TL;DR** — The repo ships a detailed methodology for how to phrase a customer outcome, how to score it, and how to lay out a job map — and then enforces none of it. You can save "make it faster" as a desired outcome. You can save an outcome with no scores at all, and the "underserved opportunity" analysis silently skips it. The eight job-map stages exist only in a React file. After this issue, one shared validator runs on **every** write — MCP tool, CLI command, Studio API route, and agent tool call — so the store only ever contains methodologically sound data, and a bad statement comes back with the sentence that would fix it.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Area** | `area/core` |
| **Priority** | `priority/high` |
| **Kind** | specification |
| **Depends on** | — |
| **Related PRs** | #62, #64, #70 |
| **Blocks** | {{ISSUE_03}}, {{ISSUE_08}}, {{ISSUE_07}} |

---

## The problem

`.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md` is the project's own source of truth for the methodology. It is explicit and it is not implemented.

**1. The outcome statement format is never validated before persistence.**
The mandated format is `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]` (`.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md:34-43`). Reality:

- `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/services.py:142-170` — `add_outcome` accepts any string.
- `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/evaluation.py:20-64` — `evaluate_outcome_statement` exists and is called from exactly **one** place: the advisory `evaluate_outcome` MCP tool (`apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:456-457`).
- The write paths that bypass it: `add_outcome` (`mcp_server.py:98`), `update_outcome` (`mcp_server.py:323`), `promote_evidence` → outcome (`services.py:313`), the CLI's `desired-outcomes add` (`apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/desired_outcomes.py:22`), and the Studio API's `POST /api/outcomes` (`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/router.py:239-263`).

**2. The validator itself is a weak proxy for the format it claims to check.**
`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/evaluation.py:20-56`:

- It **never checks for a Unit of Measure** — *"Minimize the banana when cooking"* passes.
- The object-of-control check is the literal substring `" the "` (`:37`), not a parse.
- The context check is a seven-item substring list (`:7-15`) — `", as "` and `" if "` produce false positives.
- It cannot detect solution-framed outcomes — *"Minimize the notification when alerts arrive"* is **valid**, and the guardrail file explicitly calls that a bad statement (`:41`).
- The vague-term blacklist (`:17`) is five words — *"Minimize the time to do X faster"* is wrongly flagged.

**3. Importance and satisfaction are optional, so a whole Outcome can have no score.**
`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py:53-56` — `importance: float | None = None`, `satisfaction: float | None = None`. `services.py:158-160` only computes a score when **both** are present. The consequence is severe and quiet: `OpportunityLandscape` skips any outcome with `opportunity_score === None`, so an unscored outcome is **invisible to the "underserved > 10" analysis** that the whole product is built around. The methodology requires both scores (`.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md:43`, `:119`).

**4. The Universal Job Map is not enforced anywhere.**
The eight stages — Define, Locate, Prepare, Confirm, Execute, Monitor, Modify, Conclude (`.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md:49-57`) — exist in exactly one place in the whole repository: a hardcoded array in `apps/studio/src/components/canvas/JobMap.tsx:8-15`. `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py:39-43` — `Step` is just `{job_id, name, order}`. `services.py:132-136` — `add_step` accepts any name.

Worse: `ODI_FRAMEWORK_GUIDELINES` — the string the tool `get_odi_framework_guidelines` returns, and which the guardrail file tells the agent to call (`.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md:123`) — **never mentions the eight stages at all** (`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/messages.py:30-35`).

**5. The stage order in the tool contradicts the methodology.**
`.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md` — Stage 1 Job, Stage 2 Outcomes, Stage 3 **Job Map**, Stage 4 **Opportunity Scoring**, Stage 5 Segmentation, Stage 6 Strategy.
`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/messages.py:3-43` — Stage 1 Job, Stage 2 Outcomes, Stage 3 **Calculate Opportunity Scores**, Stage 4 **Build the Job Map**.

Stages 3 and 4 are swapped. The agent is therefore routed to a *different* methodology than the one the project documents.

**6. "Outcomes before the job map" is not enforced.**
`.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md:60` — *"Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements."* `add_step` works on a job with zero outcomes. There is no ordering gate anywhere.

**7. The Studio's own prompt disagrees with the store's behaviour.**
`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:28-38` — rule 2 tells the agent to use the strict 4-part format and rule 4 says to always invoke the tools. But nothing verifies the result, so a model that ignores rule 2 writes garbage and the app accepts it.

## What a person experiences

You say to the agent: *"people hate how long it takes to onboard."* The agent composes *"Minimize the time it takes a new engineer to reach their first successful deploy."* It asks you for two numbers — how important, and how satisfied you are today — because without them the outcome cannot be compared to anything. If you try to save *"make onboarding faster"*, the agent says: *"That reads as a solution, not an outcome. The format is: direction + unit + object + context. Did you mean 'Minimize the time it takes to…'?"* Your job map shows the eight stages, and the Studio tells you *"capture some outcomes first — they are what give the map its meaning"* if you try to build a map on an empty job.

## Specification

### 6.1 One shared, strict validator

Rewrite `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/evaluation.py` into the single authority:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StatementIssue:
    code: str          # "missing_direction" | "missing_unit" | "missing_object"
                       # | "missing_context" | "solution_framed" | "too_short"
                       # | "too_long" | "vague_term"
    message: str       # human-readable
    suggestion: str | None = None

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StatementVerdict:
    valid: bool
    direction: Direction | None
    unit_of_measure: str | None
    object_of_control: str | None
    contextual_clarifier: str | None
    issues: tuple[StatementIssue, ...]

def evaluate_outcome_statement(statement: str) -> StatementVerdict: ...
def require_outcome_statement(statement: str) -> StatementVerdict:
    """Raise OutcomeStatementError with a fixable message if invalid."""
```

Rules, each with a code and a suggestion:

| Code | Rule | Example suggestion |
|---|---|---|
| `missing_direction` | Must begin with "Minimize" or "Maximize" | "Start with 'Minimize' or 'Maximize'." |
| `missing_unit` | Must contain a unit of measure — a number, a time, a count, a percentage, or a rate word (`time`, `cost`, `number`, `frequency`, `rate`, `percentage`, `time to`, `steps`, `attempts`) | "Add a unit of measure, e.g. 'time', 'cost', or 'number of …'." |
| `missing_object` | Must contain a noun phrase after the direction | "Name the object of control, e.g. 'the time it takes to …'." |
| `missing_context` | Must contain a context marker (`when`, `while`, `before`, `after`, `during`, `if`, `as`, `for`) | "Add when it happens, e.g. '… when onboarding'." |
| `solution_framed` | Must not contain solution nouns (`notification`, `dashboard`, `button`, `feature`, `screen`, `email`, `workflow`, `integration`, `report`, `toggle`) | "That names a solution. Name the customer's problem instead." |
| `vague_term` | Must not contain `better`, `improve`, `optimize`, `easier`, `nice`, `good`, `bad`, `fast` (as a bare adverb) | "Replace 'faster' with a unit, e.g. 'the time it takes'." |
| `too_short` | ≥ 6 words | — |
| `too_long` | ≤ 200 characters | — |

**Backward compatibility:** `evaluate_outcome_statement` currently returns a `dict` with `statement`, `valid`, `direction`, `issues`, `suggestions`. Change the return type to `StatementVerdict` and update the `evaluate_outcome` MCP tool's serializer (`apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:456-457`) to emit the same JSON keys plus the new fields. Existing tests that assert on the old shape must be updated in the same PR.

### 6.2 Mandatory scores

- `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py:53-56` — `importance` and `satisfaction` become **required** `float` fields on `Outcome`, validated to `1.0 ≤ x ≤ 10.0` by a Pydantic `Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)`.
- `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/services.py:142-170` — `add_outcome` requires both. The `importance`/`satisfaction` range check at `services.py:116-121` moves into the model so every path gets it.
- `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:98-121` — `add_outcome`'s `importance` and `satisfaction` parameters become **required**. Update `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py:66-69` accordingly (`required=("job_id", "statement", "importance", "satisfaction")`).
- `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/desired_outcomes.py:26-27` — `--importance` and `--satisfaction` become required options.
- `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/schemas.py:32-37` — `AddOutcomeRequest` already requires them as plain `float`; add `ge=1.0, le=10.0`.
- **Migration.** Existing rows with `NULL` scores must be backfilled, not deleted. On repository open, run a one-time migration that assigns `importance = 5.0, satisfaction = 5.0` to any outcome missing them, and records a `OUTCOME_BACKFILLED` event so the action is auditable. The Studio must show unscored backfilled outcomes in a distinct state, not silently among the scored ones.
- `promote_evidence` → outcome (`services.py:285-320`) must require both scores, or create the outcome as a **proposal** (see {{ISSUE_03}}) rather than an outcome.

### 6.3 The eight Universal Job Map stages

- Add to `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py`:

```python
class JobStage(StrEnum):
    DEFINE = "define"
    LOCATE = "locate"
    PREPARE = "prepare"
    CONFIRM = "confirm"
    EXECUTE = "execute"
    MONITOR = "monitor"
    MODIFY = "modify"
    CONCLUDE = "conclude"
```

- `Step` gains `stage: JobStage | None = None` and `stage_index: int | None = None` (1–8, the position in the canonical order).
- `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/services.py:132-140` — `add_step` gains an optional `stage`. When given, `stage_index` is derived from `JobStage` so ordering is canonical and two people cannot disagree about what "Monitor" comes after.
- `get_job_map` (`services.py:138`) returns the steps **ordered by `stage_index` when present**, falling back to `order` otherwise, and includes the canonical stage list so a client can render the eight slots whether or not they are filled.
- `apps/studio/src/components/canvas/JobMap.tsx:8-15` — **delete the hardcoded array** and import the stage list from the API. The SPA must not own domain vocabulary.
- **Ordering gate:** `add_step` on a job with **zero** outcomes must either be rejected, or accepted and flagged. The rule file says outcomes come first (`:60`). Choose **reject with a fixable message** — *"Add at least one desired outcome before building the job map; outcomes are what give the steps their meaning."* — and add an explicit escape hatch `add_step(..., allow_empty_job_map=True)` for agents that need to stage a map deliberately. The escape hatch must be recorded in the audit trail (see {{ISSUE_05}}).

### 6.4 Enforce on every write path

Introduce `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/validation.py` (or extend `evaluation.py`) exposing:

```python
def validate_outcome_write(statement, importance, satisfaction, job_id, step_id) -> None
```

which raises `OutcomeStatementError` / `ValueOutOfRangeError` with a message that says **what to do**, not just what is wrong.

Call it from **every** write path:

| Path | File | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `ODIService.add_outcome` | `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/services.py:142-170` | before the repository write |
| `ODIService.update_outcome` | `services.py:106-125` | before the write |
| `ODIService.promote_evidence` → outcome | `services.py:285-320` | before the write |
| `ODIService.add_step` | `services.py:132-140` | stage + ordering gate |
| MCP `add_outcome` / `update_outcome` | `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:98,323` | the service raises; the tool returns the message |
| CLI `desired-outcomes add` / `update` | `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/desired_outcomes.py:22` | surface the message, exit non-zero |

> "🗺️ **Build Job Maps**: Break down a Job into ordered Steps." — no mention of `update_step` / `delete_step`.
> "📊 **Track Desired Outcomes**" — no mention of `update_outcome` / `delete_outcome`.
> "📊 **Customer Outcomes**: Manage…" — no mention of `update_customer_outcome` / `delete_customer_outcome`.
> "🧾 **Evidence**" — names `add_evidence`, `list_evidence`, `promote_evidence` but not `get_evidence` or `delete_evidence`.
> `compute_opportunity` is never named. `get_capabilities` never names itself.

That is **11 of 30 tools invisible** to an agent that reads only this string.

**2. Nothing tests the sync.**
`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py:14-142` — `ToolName` (30 values), `ToolSpec`, `TOOL_SPECS`, `TOOL_NAMES`. `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py:16` asserts the live FastMCP registry's names equal `TOOL_SPECS` keys, and `:26-27` asserts the arguments and required names match. **The tool surface is protected. The human-readable description of it is not.** The only assertions on `CAPABILITIES` are substring checks in `apps/mcp-server/tests/test_odi.py:82-95` and `test_customer_outcomes.py:108`.

It omits three: `evaluate_outcome`, `get_odi_framework_guidelines`, `get_capabilities`. A terminal-only user — which the README makes a first-class path, with a binary installer and 24-hour auto-update — has **no access to the only format validator in the codebase**.

input.content:
> **TL;DR** — The repository documents six ODI stages. It implements three. Stages 5 and 6 — *segment the market by which outcomes are underserved*, and *choose a strategy: differentiated, disruptive, or new-market* — do not exist as a single line of code, anywhere. The agent can tell you a score is 15 and stop there. After this issue it can also tell you **who** is underserved, **which segment** that makes, and **what kind of bet** the evidence supports — and the reasoning is inspectable.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Area** | `area/core` |
| **Priority** | `priority/medium` |
| **Kind** | specification |
| **Depends on** | {{ISSUE_06}} (stages 1–4 must be sound first) |
| **Related PRs** | — |
| **Blocks** | {{ISSUE_18}} (a strategy is what a background agent would be given) |

---

## The problem

`.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md` defines six stages. Stages 1–4 are (imperfectly) implemented. Stages 5 and 6 are not present.

**Stage 5 — Outcome-based market segmentation** (`.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md:85-93`):

> ODI does **not** use demographic segmentation. It segments the market by **which outcomes are underserved** for each group. Segments can be Underserved, Overserved, or Appropriately served.

**Stage 6 — Formulation of an innovation strategy** (`.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md:97-107`):

> Differentiated (improve existing products for high-opportunity underserved outcomes) / Disruptive (low-cost solutions for overserved segments) / New-Market (a new job entirely unaddressed).

**Reality:**

- A grep for `disruptive`, `differentiated`, `new-market`, `new_market`, `Segment`, `segmentation` across `packages/` and `apps/` returns **nothing**.
- There is no `Segment` or `Strategy` entity in `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py:12-131`.
- There is no MCP tool, no CLI command, no API route, and no UI surface.
- The only segmentation-adjacent code is a boolean `isUnderserved(score)` in `apps/studio/src/lib/odi.ts:12-14` and an "UNDERSERVED / NORMAL" badge in `apps/studio/src/components/canvas/OpportunityLandscape.tsx:458`. That is a **per-outcome label**, not a segment.

**Why it matters more than a missing feature.** The whole product promise is *"help me choose and win the next opportunity that matters"* (`README.md`, the North Star). A score of 15 without a segment and a strategy is a number, not a decision. The agent currently cannot answer the two questions a product manager actually asks: *"who is this for?"* and *"so what do we do about it?"* — and the two questions it *can* answer ("what is the score?", "what is the map?") are the ones nobody loses sleep over.

**A second, quieter gap.** The methodology says segmentation is by *outcome cluster*, not by demographics. A naive implementation — grouping outcomes by score and calling each group a segment — is a common failure mode, because a segment is a **group of people plus a functional job** (`.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md:23`), and the outcomes are only the evidence for it. A segment built purely from score buckets would be demographic segmentation with extra steps, or worse, would look like it works and produce confident nonsense.

## What a person experiences

You have captured forty outcomes across three jobs. You ask the agent: *"who should we be building for?"* It answers with segments, not with scores:

> **Segment 1 — Platform engineers, secrets rotation**
> 3 outcomes underserved, opportunity scores 14.2 / 13.8 / 12.1. The pattern: every one of them is blocked at the *Prepare* stage — the job is understood and the resource is known, but the set-up step costs an afternoon.
> *Source outcomes:* O-14, O-19, O-27.
> **Verdict: underserved.** Build for this segment.

> **Segment 2 — Data analysts, dashboard access**
> 4 outcomes, all satisfied at 7/10. You are over-serving this group: they get the outcome today and are not asking for more.
> *Source outcomes:* O-3, O-8, O-11, O-22.
> **Verdict: overserved.** Do not invest here. Consider a lower-cost offer.

Then it proposes a strategy and says why:

> **Recommended strategy: Differentiated.**
> Segment 1 is underserved on outcomes that Segment 2 already has. The job is the same; the unmet need is not.
> *Rejected: Disruptive — Segment 2 is overserved but the job is not a full-service purchase, so a low-cost offer would not displace it.*
> *Rejected: New-Market — every outcome maps to an existing job.*

And it shows the reasoning, so you can disagree with it.

## Specification

### 8.1 Entities

Add to `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py`:

```python
class SegmentVerdict(StrEnum):
    UNDERSERVED = "underserved"
    OVERSERVED = "overserved"
    APPROPRIATELY_SERVED = "appropriately_served"

class StrategyKind(StrEnum):
    DIFFERENTIATED = "differentiated"
    DISRUPTIVE = "disruptive"
    NEW_MARKET = "new_market"

class Segment(BaseModel):
    id: str
    job_id: str | None = None
    name: str                       # human label, e.g. "Platform engineers, secrets rotation"
    people: str                     # the group, described in the person's words
    job_statement: str              # the functional job in their words
    outcome_ids: list[str]          # the evidence for this segment
    verdict: SegmentVerdict
    rationale: str
    confidence: float               # 0.0 - 1.0
    created_at: datetime

class Strategy(BaseModel):
    id: str
    kind: StrategyKind
    segment_id: str | None
    thesis: str                     # one paragraph
    bets: list[str]                 # proposed moves
    rejected: list[dict]            # [{"kind": "disruptive", "why": "..."}]
    created_at: datetime
```

`Segment.verdict` is **derived**, not stored arbitrarily — see 8.2.

### 8.2 Deriving the verdict from outcomes

The verdict is a computation over the segment's outcomes, and the formula must be explicit and inspectable:

```python
def segment_verdict(outcomes: Sequence[Outcome]) -> SegmentVerdict:
    """Classify a segment by the opportunity scores of its outcomes.

    Underserved        — at least one outcome with opportunity_score > 10
    Appropriately served — every outcome with a score, and all scores <= 10
    Overserved         — every outcome's satisfaction >= its importance
                          (the customer already has the outcome)
    """
```

- **Underserved** — at least one outcome scoring `> 10`. This is the existing threshold from `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py:28-30` and `apps/studio/src/lib/odi.ts:8-14`. Reuse the threshold; do not invent a second one.
- **Overserved** — every outcome has `satisfaction >= importance`. The customer already has what they need.
- **Appropriately served** — scored, and none above 10.
- A segment with **any unscored outcome** cannot be classified. `Segment.verdict` must be optional, and the UI must say "not enough signal", not guess. {{ISSUE_06}} backfills legacy rows, but new rows always have both scores.

### 8.3 Clustering outcomes into candidate segments

This is the part that must not be faked. Implement it as a pluggable strategy, like {{ISSUE_03}}'s proposal strategy:

```python
class SegmentationStrategy(Protocol):
    def segment(self, jobs: Sequence[Job], outcomes: Sequence[Outcome]) -> list[Segment]: ...
```

Ship one default implementation, `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/segmentation.py::OutcomeClusterStrategy`:

1. **Group by job.** Outcomes belong to a job (`Outcome.job_id`). A segment is scoped to a job, because a job is the functional unit (`.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md:25`).
2. **Group by step.** Within a job, outcomes that attach to the same `step_id` are candidates for the same segment — because the same step is the same point of friction for the same people. Use the canonical `JobStage` from {{ISSUE_06}}.
3. **Name the segment from the evidence.** The `name` is composed as `"<the people>, <the job>"` using the job's name and the segment's dominant step. The `people` field must be the **person's own words** if they are recorded (the brief's `target_user`, `apps/studio-api/.../studio/schemas.py`), and must otherwise be derived from the outcome statements' shared object of control — and must be labeled as inferred.
4. **Compute the verdict** with `segment_verdict`.
5. **Set `confidence` from the evidence**: the fraction of the segment's outcomes that share a dominant step, and the number of outcomes (a segment built from one outcome is a hypothesis, not a segment).
6. **A segment must have at least two outcomes to be a segment.** A single outcome is reported as an *unclustered outcome*, listed separately, so a lone outcome is never inflated into a market.

The strategy must be deterministic, offline, and unit-testable with fixed inputs and fixed outputs.

**Anti-pattern to avoid explicitly:** do not cluster by demographics, by industry, by company size, or by score magnitude alone. `.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md:87` forbids demographic segmentation, and the guardrail table at `:121` says to use outcome-based logic. Add a test that the strategy's output is invariant to any demographic field present in the inputs.

### 8.4 Strategy formulation

`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/strategy.py::propose_strategy(segments, jobs, outcomes) -> Strategy`:

- **Differentiated** — proposed when at least one segment is underserved **and** its outcomes relate to a job that already has served outcomes. The thesis names the underserved outcome and the served one it can be borrowed from.
- **Disruptive** — proposed when a segment is overserved. The thesis must name what the segment would do with a *cheaper, simpler* offer, and must state that the job is not a full-service purchase (or note that it is, which weakens the case).
- **New-Market** — proposed when outcomes exist that **map to no existing job**. This is detectable: an outcome whose job is not a served job. The thesis must name the new job.
- **The output must always include the rejected alternatives and why.** A strategy without its rejections is a conclusion, not a recommendation. `Strategy.rejected` is a required list with one entry per non-chosen kind.
- **Exactly one strategy is recommended.** The others are recorded as rejected. The agent may present more than one, but the data model records one.

### 8.5 Service, persistence, tools, API, CLI

- `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/services.py` — add to `ODIService`:
  - `segment_market(job_id: str | None = None) -> list[Segment]`
  - `list_segments() -> list[Segment]`
  - `propose_strategy(segment_ids: list[str] | None = None) -> Strategy`
  - `list_strategies() -> list[Strategy]`
  - `save_segment(segment)`, `save_strategy(strategy)` — persist a computed result so it is reviewable and can be referenced later.
- Extend the `Repository` protocol, `InMemoryRepository`, and `SQLiteRepository` with `add_segment`, `get_segment`, `list_segments`, `update_segment`, `add_strategy`, `get_strategy`, `list_strategies`.
- Event types `SEGMENT_CREATED`, `STRATEGY_CREATED` in `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/sqlite_repository.py:51-112`.
- **MCP tools** (add to `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py` and to `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py`):
  - `get_segments(job_id: str | None = None) -> list[Segment]`
  - `get_strategy() -> Strategy | None`
  - `propose_strategy(job_id: str | None = None) -> Strategy`
- **API routes** (both backends, per `router.py:51-52`):
  - `GET /api/segments`
  - `GET /api/strategy`
  - `POST /api/strategy/propose`
- **CLI** — a `segments` command group (`list`, `show`) and a `strategy` command group (`show`, `propose`); register in `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/cli.py:29-41`; add the local handlers to `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/backend.py:460-488` — remembering that {{ISSUE_07}} tightens the contract to require the handler set to **equal** `TOOL_NAMES`.

### 8.6 The prompt

`packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/messages.py:3-43` — `ODI_FRAMEWORK_GUIDELINES` must gain Stage 5 and Stage 6 (and its stage order is fixed by {{ISSUE_06}}). {{ISSUE_06}} rewrites this string; **this issue extends it, and the two must not both edit it concurrently.** Whichever lands second updates the other's test.

Text for the new stages:

```
### Stage 5: Segment by Underserved Outcomes
- **When**: After outcomes are scored.
- **Never** segment by demographics. A segment is a group of people plus a functional job.
- **Tools**: `get_segments(job_id?)`, `propose_strategy()`.
- A segment is underserved when one of its outcomes scores above 10, and overserved when
  the customer already has the outcome (satisfaction at or above importance).

### Stage 6: Formulate the Innovation Strategy
- **When**: After segments are clear.
- **Differentiated**: improve an existing product for an underserved segment.
- **Disruptive**: offer a lower-cost solution to an overserved segment.
- **New-Market**: create for a job no one is being served on today.
- **Tools**: `propose_strategy(job_id?)`.
- Always state the strategies you rejected and why.
```

`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:28-38` — add a rule telling the agent to answer *"who is this for?"* with segments and *"so what do we do?"* with a strategy, and to name the rejected alternatives.

### 8.7 UI surfaces

- **A `segment` card type** in `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` + `apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx`:
  - the segment's name, the people, the job statement, the verdict, the confidence, the source outcomes, and the rationale;
  - the verdict must be visually distinct per class (underserved / overserved / appropriately served) and must **never** be shown without the confidence;
  - an outcome that could not be clustered is shown in a separate "Unclustered" group, not silently dropped.
- **A `strategy` card type**:
  - the recommended strategy, the thesis, the proposed bets, and the **rejected alternatives with their reasons**;
  - a strategy card with no rejected alternatives is invalid and must be rejected by the server-side validator (`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/ui_spec.py:106-155`).
- **A canvas lens** — `apps/studio/src/components/workspace/panels.tsx:34-98` — add a `segments` lens showing every segment with its verdict, and make it reachable from `apps/studio/src/components/workspace/WorkbenchRail.tsx` and from a `/segments` slash command in `apps/studio/src/lib/commands.ts:38-123`.

### 8.8 The methodology guardrail must be testable

The repo's own guardrail table (`.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md:121`) says: *"Use outcome-based logic to identify market segments. Do **not** use demographics or assumptions."* Add a test that asserts the segmentation strategy's output is **invariant** to any demographic attribute, and a test that a segment built from a single outcome is reported as unclustered.

## Non-negotiable constraints

- **No demographic segmentation.** The segment's unit of analysis is the outcome, and the segment is scoped to a job.
- The `> 10` underserved threshold is the one already in `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py:28-30`. There is exactly one.
- A segment with fewer than two outcomes is not a segment.
- A segment that cannot be classified (any unscored outcome) is reported as unclassified, never guessed.
- The strategy output must include the rejected alternatives.
- The default strategy is deterministic, offline, and unit-testable.
- Confidence is always visible next to a verdict.

## Out of scope

- Demographic or firmographic attributes of any kind.
- A clustering model that requires a network or an LLM (the protocol allows one later).
- Automated market sizing or revenue projection.
- Competitive analysis.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Segment`, `SegmentVerdict`, `Strategy`, and `StrategyKind` exist in `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py` and are exported from `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/__init__.py`.
- [ ] `segment_verdict()` implements underserved / overserved / appropriately-served with the existing `> 10` threshold.

- [ ] The default segmentation strategy groups by job and step, requires ≥ 2 outcomes, and is deterministic.
- [ ] A test proves the strategy's output is invariant to demographic attributes.
- [ ] A test proves a single outcome is reported as unclustered, not as a segment.
- [ ] `propose_strategy` returns exactly one strategy and always populates `rejected` with one entry per non-chosen kind.
- [ ] `Repository`, `InMemoryRepository`, and `SQLiteRepository` persist segments and strategies; SQLite is event-sourced.
- [ ] `get_segments`, `get_strategy`, and `propose_strategy` exist as MCP tools and are registered in the contract.
- [ ] `GET /api/segments`, `GET /api/strategy`, `POST /api/strategy/propose` work under both backends.

- [ ] `ODI_FRAMEWORK_GUIDELINES` contains Stage 5 and Stage 6 in the canonical order, and the parity test against `.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md` covers them.
- [ ] `segment` and `strategy` card types exist; a `strategy` card with no rejected alternatives is rejected by the server-side validator.
- [ ] A `segments` lens exists and is reachable from the rail and from a `/segments` command.

uv run --directory apps/studio-api pytest

> **TL;DR** — Six of the seven open pull requests on this repository contain a single commit that quietly replaces the whole tree with an old snapshot, deleting nine to eleven features that were already merged. They pass CI, because the reverted tree is internally consistent. Their descriptions are also materially false — one claims "20 touch-first improvements" and ships three CSS blocks and five tests; another claims to "delegate knowledge storage to external systems" and adds a URL field. After this issue, a pull request that deletes a file that exists on `main`, or whose description does not match its diff, fails CI before a human ever reads it.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Area** | `area/ci` |
| **Priority** | `priority/high` |
| **Kind** | specification |
| **Depends on** | — |
| **Related PRs** | #62, #63, #64, #65, #66, #70 |
| **Blocks** | {{ISSUE_10}} |

---

## The problem

**The pattern.** Every one of the six machine-generated branches (`google-labs-jules[bot]`) contains a *tree-replacement* commit — one commit touching 100+ files with roughly 20,000 deletions, dated 20:40–20:43, applied to branches whose real work was committed at 15:53–16:15.

| PR | Branch | Real work (first commit) | Tree-replacement commit | Net deletions |

| #66 | `feat/mobile-ux-elevation-…` | `d28d6a6e` — 7 files, +163/−7 | `fcccb4d0` — 158 files, +1981/−21830 | −21,715 |
| #65 | `feat/on-device-llm-fallback-router-…` | `3ff731b8` — 10 files, +382/−1 | `713a8cd2` — 161 files, +1758/−22013 | −21,825 |
| #64 | `feat/v2mom-context-capture-…` | `cf8e9489` — 11 files, +114/−5 | `76192e1b` — 108 files, +1327/−12939 | −12,926 |
| #63 | `jules-12210456461843385903-14563de9` | `3714baee` — 4 files, +7/−3 | `040a65a5` — 157 files, +1668/−21747 | −21,745 |
| #62 | `feat/cloud-agent-work-scheduling-…` | `f849c394` — 27 files, +1699/−5 | `75b60e08` — 105 files, +1332/−13594 | −12,924 |

**What those tree-replacement commits delete** — features that were already merged and shipped:

| Deleted file | Feature it carried | Merged in |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/flags.py`, `settings.py` | feature flags | #72 |
| `apps/studio-api/.../studio/changelog.py` | the changelog drawer | #60 |
| `apps/studio-api/.../studio/connectors.py` | MCP ↔ Studio connectors | #56 |
| `apps/studio-api/.../studio/ui_spec.py` | generative UI surfaces | #55 |
| `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts`, `cards.tsx`, `protocol.ts` | the generative UI protocol | #55 |
| `apps/studio/src/onboarding/FirstRunWizard.tsx` | the first-run wizard | #69 |
| `apps/studio/src/components/notifications/CatchUpFeed.tsx` | catch-up notifications | #58 |
| `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/events.py`, `tests/test_events.py` | the event-sourced store | #42 |
| `apps/studio/src/components/setup/SetupConversation.tsx` | the context conversation | #43 |

Merging **any one** of the six would silently revert all of the above. `apps/studio/src/styles/theme.css` drops from 3,094 lines to 557–2,207 depending on the branch.

**Why CI did not catch it.** The six branches are internally consistent — the reverted tree compiles and its own tests pass. `ci.yml` has no job that looks at the *shape* of a diff. The only structural guard is the "Verify generated API types are up to date" step in the `studio` job, and it does not fire for deletions of files that are not API types.

**Why the descriptions did not catch it.** The PR bodies are machine-generated and materially false:

- #66 claims "20 touch-first micro-improvements" and "Vitest Unit Tests … 29 total tests passing" — the branch has **5** tests. It claims a mobile slide-over drawer built on `ChatCopilot.tsx`, a header switcher in `StudioHeader.tsx`, and swipeable tabs in `CanvasTabs.tsx` — **none of those three files exist on `main`**. It claims "All 546 pytest suite tests pass" while *deleting* seven test files.
- #65 claims an "on-device LLM fallback and multi-tier model router" — the "LLM" is a four-branch keyword matcher; `router.py:39-41` is `def is_available(self) -> bool: return True`; the diff adds **zero dependencies**; and `docs/local-llm.md` §6 promises a Settings UI and a config file for the routing mode, neither of which exists.
- #64 claims the assistant "continuously detects and refines V2MOM artifacts" — the entire change is **one line of prompt text**. There is no detection, extraction, or refinement code.
- #62 claims "cloud agent work scheduling" — `services.py:391` on that branch writes `"Executed mock cloud agent task '{work.name}' successfully"` and sets `status=COMPLETED`. No agent is dispatched. The CLI advertises ISO, relative and cron expressions; **none of the three is parsed**.
- #70 claims "delegation of full knowledge storage to external systems" — nothing delegates. The diff adds a `url: str | None` field.

**A human reviewing only the bodies would approve all six.**

**And the ruleset does not help.** The `main-requires-ci-green` ruleset has `bypass_actors: [{actor_id: 5, actor_type: RepositoryRole, bypass_mode: "always"}]` — the repository owner can merge to `main` with the check unsatisfied, with no warning. And `strict_required_status_checks_policy: false` means a branch that has never run CI can satisfy the check. #70 and #64 currently have **no `CI green` run on their head SHA**; they are blocked only because the owner has not used the bypass.

## What a person experiences

A pull request arrives. Before a human reads it, CI has already asked the two questions that matter: *"does this delete anything that is already shipped?"* and *"does the description match what the code does?"* A PR that reverts eleven merged features fails with a list of exactly which files it would remove and which release they shipped in. A PR that says it delivers twenty improvements and delivers three fails with a diff of the discrepancy. The reviewer reads a body they can trust, because a machine checked it.

## Specification

### 9.1 A diff-shape gate

Add `.github/workflows/pr-guardrails.yml`, triggered on `pull_request`. It must not need any secrets, and it must not be bypassable by a ruleset.

**Gate 1 — deletion budget.** A pull request must not delete a file that exists on the base branch, unless the deletion is explicitly allowed.

- Compute the set of files deleted relative to the base (`git diff --diff-filter=D --name-only origin/${{ github.base_ref }}...HEAD`).
- The gate **fails** if any deleted file is not in an allowlist.
- The allowlist is a YAML file at `.github/pr-guardrails/deletion-allowlist.yml`:
  ```yaml
  # One entry per approved deletion, with the reason and the issue that tracks it.
  - path: "apps/old/thing.tsx"
    issue: "#123"
    reason: "Replaced by apps/new/thing.tsx in #123"
  ```
- **Default deny.** An empty allowlist means no deletions are permitted.
- The message must list each deleted file and the release it shipped in, so the failure is actionable.

**Gate 2 — diff size.** A pull request must not exceed a deletion budget.

- `deletions > 500` in the total diff → fail, with a message asking the author to split the change.
- The threshold is configurable via `.github/pr-guardrails/config.yml` (`max_deletions`, `max_changed_files`).
- The check must **exclude** files that are legitimately regenerated (lockfiles, `openapi.json`, `schema.d.ts`, `coverage.xml`) via an explicit exclusion list — those are already generated and drifted by design.
- **The check must run on the cumulative PR diff, not per commit.** A tree-replacement commit buried in the middle of a branch is still visible in the cumulative diff. This is the whole point: all six broken PRs pass on a per-commit basis if you only look at the last commit.

**Gate 3 — branch freshness.** A pull request whose base is behind `origin/main` by more than N commits (default 50) must rebase. This does not catch the tree-replacement commit by itself, but it forces the rebase that would expose the conflict, and it is a cheap early signal. **This gate must be a warning, not a failure**, because rebases produce conflicts that a human resolves better.

### 9.2 A body-truth gate

A pull request description is a specification. It must match the diff.

- Extract the PR body (`github.event.pull_request.body`).
- **Rule 1 — file count.** If the body contains a claim of the form "N files" or "N+ files" (including a table of "micro-improvements" with N numbered rows), the gate counts the files actually changed and fails if the numbers differ by more than a small tolerance (default 20%). This catches #63 (claims 20 improvements, changes 4 files) and #66 (claims 20 improvements, changes 164 files but only 7 in the real commit).
- **Rule 2 — test-count claims.** If the body contains "N tests passing" or "N total tests", the gate counts the test functions added in the diff (`it(`, `test_`, `def test_`) and fails if the claim is off by more than 20%. This catches #66's "29 total tests" against 5.
- **Rule 3 — named-file claims.** If the body names a source file (a path with a recognizable extension), the gate asserts the file exists in the diff **or** exists on the base branch. This catches #66's claims about `ChatCopilot.tsx`, `StudioHeader.tsx`, and `CanvasTabs.tsx`, none of which exist.
- **Rule 4 — numbers in the title.** If the title contains "N " followed by a noun such as improvements, micro-improvements, features, or tests, the same file-count check applies.
- The gate emits a **warning comment** on the PR (not a failure) for rules 1–4, because natural language is hard to parse and a false positive is expensive. **The failure is reserved for the diff-shape gate**, which is deterministic.
- A companion script, `scripts/pr_guards.py`, holds the logic so it is unit-testable. Tests live in `tests/scripts/test_pr_guards.py`.

### 9.3 A fabrication guard on the code itself

A separate check, in the same workflow, greps the diff for patterns that have actually shipped in this repository's history:

- `mock` in a docstring or a comment **on a line that also returns a fabricated value** — for example `services.py:391`'s `"Executed mock cloud agent task"`.
- `is_available` implementations that `return True` unconditionally.
- Hardcoded numeric "result" strings that look like a measurement (`"3,000 hours of developer agony"`).
- A `TODO`, `FIXME`, `NotImplementedError`, or `pass  # stub` in a **new** line of the diff.

This check reports a **warning** with the file and line, and links to the issue that must resolve it. It does not block, because a legitimate word "mock" in a test file must not fail a build. Exclude `**/tests/**` and `**/test_*.py`.

### 9.4 The ruleset must be tightened

- The `main-requires-ci-green` ruleset must set `strict_required_status_checks_policy: true`, so a branch that has never run CI cannot satisfy the check.
- The admin bypass must be changed from `bypass_mode: "always"` to `bypass_mode: "pull_request"` (or removed). **A bypass that is always on is not a gate.**
- A **second required check** is added to the ruleset: `PR guardrails` (the workflow from 9.1). A PR that deletes shipped files must not be mergeable, even by an admin.
- **Note for the implementer:** ruleset changes are repository settings, not files. Do them with `gh api` / the API, and record the change in `docs/architecture/README.md` so it is not lost. `gh api repos/alehar9320/agentic-odi/rulesets` lists the current ruleset (`id 25356329`).

### 9.5 A merge template that asks the right questions

Update `.github/pull_request_template.md` to require:

- **What a person experiences** — the user-visible change, in user terms. Not a list of files.
- **How this was verified** — the exact commands that were run, and their output.
- **What this does NOT do** — the explicit scope boundary.
- **For machine-generated work:** a **Diff summary** line stating the true file count, the true test count, and the true net line delta, and a **Mock/stub disclosure** listing anything simulated.

A template that asks for the true numbers makes the body-truth gate's job easier and makes the human's job faster.

### 9.6 A machine-readable "what this PR really does" artifact

`.github/pull_request_template.md` gains a fenced block:

````markdown
```json
{"changed_files": 7, "tests_added": 5, "net_lines": 156, "simulated": [], "breaking": []}
```
````

The gate parses it, compares it against the actual diff, and fails on a mismatch of more than the tolerance. This is deterministic and becomes the primary signal; the natural-language rules in 9.2 are the fallback for PRs that omit the block.

## Non-negotiable constraints

- **The gate must run on the cumulative PR diff.** A per-commit check does not catch the tree-replacement pattern and is not sufficient.
- The gate must work on a fork's pull request with **no secrets available**.
- The default is **deny all deletions**. The allowlist is opt-in and every entry names an issue.
- The body-truth rules produce **warnings**; only the diff-shape rules and the JSON block mismatch **fail**.
- The gate must not fail on legitimately regenerated files (lockfiles, `openapi.json`, `schema.d.ts`).
- The ruleset must end up with `strict_required_status_checks_policy: true` and a non-`always` admin bypass.
- The gate must be unit-tested; the logic lives in `scripts/pr_guards.py`, not in YAML.

## Out of scope

- Reviewing the *quality* of a change — that is a human's job and a different skill.
- Auto-approving a PR. The gate blocks; it never approves.
- The "land the real work" work itself → {{ISSUE_10}}.
- A general-purpose linter for PR descriptions. The rules are narrow and specific to the failures observed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.github/workflows/pr-guardrails.yml` runs on `pull_request` and needs no secrets.
- [ ] It fails when the PR deletes a file that exists on the base branch and is not in `.github/pr-guardrails/deletion-allowlist.yml`.
- [ ] The failure message names each deleted file and the release it shipped in.
- [ ] It fails when the total diff deletes more than 500 lines, excluding an explicit generated-file exclusion list.
- [ ] The check is computed on the cumulative PR diff, not per commit. A test proves a mid-branch tree-replacement commit is caught.
