- [ ] The JSON "what this PR really does" block is compared against the real diff and fails on a mismatch beyond the tolerance.
- [ ] The fabrication guard warns on a fabricated result string, an unconditional `is_available`, and a new `TODO`/`FIXME`/`NotImplementedError`.
- [ ] The `main-requires-ci-green` ruleset has `strict_required_status_checks_policy: true`.
- [ ] The admin bypass is no longer `always`.
- [ ] `PR guardrails` is a required status check on `main`.
- [ ] `.github/pull_request_template.md` requires "What a person experiences", "How this was verified", "What this does NOT do", and the JSON diff-summary block.
- [ ] `scripts/pr_guards.py` exists and is unit-tested in `tests/scripts/test_pr_guards.py`.

## Verification

```bash

uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .

# Manual: open a throwaway PR that deletes a file from main and confirm it fails
```

> **TL;DR** — Six machine-generated pull requests are open. Each contains one good commit followed by one commit that wipes the repository back to an old snapshot. The good parts are worth keeping: a URL field on evidence, a real mobile CSS pass, a model router, a V2MOM model, a copy pass, and a scheduling foundation. This issue says exactly what to salvage from each, how to land it as a small reviewable pull request, and what still has to be built afterwards — so none of the good work is lost and none of the damage is merged.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Area** | `area/ci`, `area/core`, `area/studio` |
| **Priority** | `priority/high` |
| **Kind** | specification |
| **Depends on** | {{ISSUE_09}} (the guardrails must be in place before the re-lands land) |
| **Related PRs** | #62, #63, #64, #65, #66, #70 |
| **Blocks** | {{ISSUE_17}}, {{ISSUE_19}} |

---

## The problem

Six of the seven open pull requests carry a tree-replacement commit that deletes nine to eleven already-merged features. They are `MERGEABLE` with green CI. A single accidental click merges a revert of #42, #43, #55, #56, #58, #60, #69, and #72.

But the *first* commit on each branch is real, small, and worth keeping. The work is not lost — it is **stranded behind a destructive commit**.

| PR | First commit (keep) | Size | Tree-replacement commit (drop) |
|---|---|---|---|
| #70 | `81f99a80` | 21 files, +1001/−26 | `c5198e55` (107 files, −13,524) |
| #66 | `d28d6a6e` | 7 files, +163/−7 | `fcccb4d0` (158 files, −21,830) |
| #65 | `3ff731b8` | 10 files, +382/−1 | `713a8cd2` (161 files, −22,013) |
| #64 | `cf8e9489` | 11 files, +114/−5 | `76192e1b` (108 files, −12,939) |
| #63 | `3714baee` | 4 files, +7/−3 | `040a65a5` (157 files, −21,747) |
| #62 | `f849c394` | 27 files, +1699/−5 | `75b60e08` (105 files, −13,594) |

Two branches also add a **root `package.json` and `package-lock.json`** with the same path and different content (#66 and #62) — a guaranteed conflict whichever order they land in. #66 additionally commits a `node_modules/` symlink, which `.gitignore` does not exclude (gitignore patterns do not match symlinks).

## What a person experiences

Each salvage lands as its own small pull request with an honest description, a real diff, and a clear statement of what it does **not** do. A person reviewing the mobile work sees seven files, not a 21,000-line revert. A person reviewing the scheduling work sees a domain entity and a set of tools — clearly labelled as a foundation with no scheduler yet, because that is what it is. The six original pull requests are then closed with a comment pointing at their replacements, so no work silently disappears and no one is left wondering what happened.

## Specification

### 10.1 The procedure

For each of the six, in this order:

1. `git checkout -b salvage/<pr>-<slug> origin/main`
2. `git cherry-pick <first-commit>` — **only the first commit.** If it conflicts, resolve by hand against `origin/main`; do not merge the branch.
3. Fix the specific defects listed for that PR below.
4. Run the full CI gate locally.
5. Open a pull request with the template from {{ISSUE_09}}, including the JSON diff-summary block.
6. Close the original pull request with a comment: *"Superseded by #N. The original branch contained a tree-replacement commit that deleted N shipped files. The real work — commit `<sha>` — has been re-landed on `main` as #N."*

**Never merge the original branches. Never rebase them onto `main` wholesale** — a rebase replays the tree-replacement commit and reproduces the damage.

### 10.2 Per-PR salvage specification

#### #70 → `salvage/evidence-url` (from `81f99a80`)

**Keep:** `Evidence.url` in `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py`; `add_evidence(..., url=...)` in `services.py`; the `"url"` entry in the evidence tool spec in `contract.py`; URL extraction from `url`/`html_url`/`link`/`uri` in `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/mapping.py`; `POST /evidence`, `DELETE /evidence/{id}`, `POST /evidence/{id}/promote` in the Studio router; the `EvidenceStream` and `OutcomeCard` changes; the TS types and API client changes; the regenerated `openapi.json` and `schema.d.ts`.

**Fix before landing:**

**The salvage is optional.** If the honest version of this is too thin to be worth a pull request, close #65 and start from {{ISSUE_17}}. That is a legitimate outcome of this issue and must be recorded in the issue.

**Keep:** the `V2MOM` Pydantic model in `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py`; its registration in `schema.py`; `StudioBrief.v2mom` in `apps/studio-api/.../studio/schemas.py`; the `_brief_lines()` changes in `chat.py`; the TS types and setup-form plumbing.

input.content:
> **TL;DR** — The README promises a 90% coverage floor, and Codecov is configured to check it — but Codecov's upload is explicitly non-blocking (`fail_ci_if_error: false`), and a fork's pull request has no token, so the check silently never fires. Locally, `pytest` runs with no floor at all. After this issue, a pull request that drops coverage below 90% fails in CI, in a job that needs no secrets, before Codecov is ever involved.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Area** | `area/ci` |
| **Priority** | `priority/medium` |
| **Kind** | specification |
| **Depends on** | — |
| **Related PRs** | — |

---

## The problem

**The claim.** `README.md` (Testing → Test Coverage) states the Codecov project status *"requires at least 90% coverage (target: 90%) and tolerates a 1% dip"*. `codecov.yml` sets `project.default.target: 90%` with `threshold: 1%`.

**The reality.**

- `pyproject.toml:37-46` — `[tool.coverage.run]` sets `source` but there is **no `[tool.coverage.report] fail_under`**. `git grep "fail_under"` across every `*.toml`, `*.yml`, and `*.cfg` in the repository returns **nothing**.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the `test` job runs `uv run pytest --cov=… --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml`. There is **no `--cov-fail-under`**.
- The Codecov upload step has `fail_ci_if_error: false` (line ~150 of the workflow) and is conditional on `matrix.python-version == '3.12'`.
- The Codecov upload needs `secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN`. A fork's pull request has no secret, so the upload is skipped and the status is never reported.
- `codecov.yml` sets `patch.default.informational: true` — new code is explicitly **not** held to a standard.

So the floor exists only on the service that has already been configured not to fail the build. The `ci-green` aggregator requires the `test` job to succeed — but the `test` job cannot fail on coverage.

**Why this matters more than usual right now.** The six machine-generated branches **delete test files** while claiming to add tests. #66's body says "All 546 pytest suite tests pass" while removing `test_studio_ui_spec.py` (−347), `test_studio_chat_ui.py` (−251), `test_studio_connectors.py` (−114), `test_studio_connectors_router.py` (−141), `test_studio_manual_crud.py` (−102), `test_studio_brief.py` (−67), and `test_events.py` (−59) — a net **decrease** in the suite. A coverage floor enforced in a secret-free job would have flagged that immediately.

There is also a history here: commit `1c4c9866` — *"test: raise combined coverage to 99% and enforce a 90% floor"* — is on `main` and added the Codecov target. The `fail_under` half of that commit did not survive the repository restructure into `apps/` and `packages/`.

**Second gap: the front end has no floor at all.** `apps/studio` has Vitest, and `codecov.yml` ignores `apps/studio/**`. The front end has 267+ tests and is the largest part of the product by line count, with no coverage measurement at all. The `ui/` protocol — the strongest part of the codebase — is validated by a registry-parity test, but nothing measures the rest.

## What a person experiences

A pull request lands. CI runs the test suite and reports one number: **"91.2% (floor 90%)"**. If the change drops it to 88%, the job fails with the exact files that lost coverage, so the author knows where to add tests rather than being told "add more tests". A person adding a feature knows the bar before they start, because the bar is in the README, in `pyproject.toml`, and in CI — the same number in all three.

## Specification

### 11.1 A local floor, enforced in the test job

- `pyproject.toml` — add:

```toml
[tool.coverage.report]
fail_under = 90
show_missing = true
skip_covered = true
```

This makes `uv run pytest --cov=…` fail locally when coverage drops below 90% — which is the behavior developers expect and which costs nothing to run.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the `test` job — add `--cov-fail-under=90` to the pytest invocation so the failure is explicit in CI output and does not depend on the coverage report plugin's exit code. `--cov-fail-under` is the pytest-cov flag; `--cov-fail-under` is what makes the `test` job itself red.

- **The floor must be measured the same way CI measures it.** The `test` job runs a single `pytest` over `testpaths = ["apps", "packages", "tests", "website"]` (the `pyproject.toml` setting) with a combined `--cov` over all five distributions. The floor applies to that combined number. Do not measure per-package and average.

### 11.2 A secret-free, fork-safe gate

- The `test` job needs no secrets today, and the coverage floor must not introduce one. `CODECOV_TOKEN` stays for the upload only.
- **The floor must fail a fork's pull request.** Because the floor is enforced by pytest's exit code in the `test` job, it does — no token required. This is the whole point of putting it there rather than relying on Codecov.
- `codecov.yml` — keep `project.default.target: 90%` and `threshold: 1%` so the Codecov badge and the PR comment reflect the same bar, but the **authoritative** gate is now the `test` job. Update the comment at the top of `codecov.yml` to say the floor is enforced in CI by pytest and that Codecov is the reporting surface.

### 11.3 The front end gets a floor too

- `apps/studio/package.json` — add a coverage configuration and a script:
  - `"test:coverage": "vitest run --coverage"` with `@vitest/coverage-v8` as a dev dependency.
  - `apps/studio/vite.config.ts` — the `test` block sets `coverage: { provider: "v8", reporter: ["text", "lcov"], thresholds: { lines: 80, functions: 80, branches: 70, statements: 80 } }`.
- **The front-end thresholds are lower than the Python floor, deliberately.** The SPA has a large untested surface (see the list below). An 80% line threshold with a ratchet is honest; a 90% threshold would fail on day one and train people to ignore the gate. **The numbers must be set to the current actual coverage, and the gate must not be loosened after that.**
- Record the current actual numbers in `apps/studio/package.json` as a comment, or in `docs/architecture/testing.md`.
- `codecov.yml` — remove `apps/studio/**` from the `ignore` list **once** the front-end coverage is uploaded, and add a Codecov upload step to the `studio` job. This is a follow-up within the same issue, not a separate one.

### 11.4 A ratchet, not a cliff

A fixed floor invites gaming. Two mechanisms prevent it:

- **The floor never goes down.** Add a CI step that reads the current coverage number and compares it to the floor; if the floor in `pyproject.toml` is **lower** than the floor in `main`, the job fails with *"the coverage floor may not be lowered"*. This is a three-line check and it is the single most valuable line in the issue.
- **Per-package visibility.** The combined number can hide a package that collapsed. Publish the per-package breakdown as a CI artifact or a job summary: a step that runs coverage per distribution and appends a table to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. The aggregate gates; the table informs.

### 11.5 The coverage map must be generated, not maintained by hand

`README.md` has a hand-maintained **Test Coverage Map** table listing what each test file covers. It is already stale — it describes the pre-restructure layout (`core/tests/…`, `mcp_server/tests/…`, `local_server/tests/…`, `client/tests/…`) rather than the current `apps/` and `packages/` layout, and it does not mention the many test files that now exist.

- **Generate the map.** A script, `scripts/coverage_map.py`, walks the test directories, pairs each test file with the source files it exercises (by import path and by name), and emits the Markdown table.
- A test asserts the generated table matches the committed `docs/architecture/testing.md` and the README section. A CI step regenerates and fails on drift — the same pattern as the existing "Verify generated API types are up to date" step in `ci.yml`.
- **Do not delete the README section**; the repo's own guardrail (`.agents/rules/agent_instructions.md:160`) requires the README to stay current. Make it generated instead of hand-written.

### 11.6 The gaps the map will expose

The map will make visible the coverage holes the repository currently has. **Record them in the issue, do not fix them here** — but they must be listed, because a coverage map that hides the holes is worse than none:

Front end, no test file at all: `src/state/StudioContext.tsx` (1,021 lines — the SSE dispatcher at `:717-782` is the heart of the client), `src/components/chat/Hero.tsx`, `src/components/chat/OfflineNotice.tsx`, `src/components/chat/Markdown.tsx`, `src/components/setup/SetupConversation.tsx` (509 lines), `src/components/canvas/DirectCapture.tsx`, `src/components/canvas/EvidenceStream.tsx`, `src/components/canvas/OutcomeCard.tsx`, `src/components/layout/StudioBar.tsx`, `src/components/Toasts.tsx`, `src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx`, `src/components/Skeletons.tsx`, `src/onboarding/storage.ts`, `src/onboarding/steps.tsx`, `src/onboarding/content.ts`, `src/ui/actions.ts`, `src/ui/props.ts`, `src/ui/catalog.ts`, `src/lib/useMediaQuery.ts`, `src/api/schema.d.ts` (dead — nothing imports it).

Untested behaviors: the `ui` SSE event arriving and being re-validated, the `connector` SSE event, `canvas_dirty` → `refreshCanvas()`, the `error` SSE event, abort/stop-streaming, the card-action → `sendMessage` round trip, and the mobile-sheet versus desktop-dock lens split (`useMediaQuery` returns `false` under jsdom, so only one branch is ever exercised).

Back end, uncovered paths: `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` exhaustion (`apps/studio-api/.../studio/chat.py:26,373`), MCP unreachable inside `stream_chat` (`:259-260`), the LLM completion call raising (`:270`), `render_ui` with `catalog is None` (`:324-330`), and the changelog regex parser (`apps/studio-api/.../studio/changelog.py:25-84`).

## Non-negotiable constraints

- **The floor is enforced by the test job's exit code**, not by Codecov, so it works on forks and when the upload fails.
- The floor measures the **combined** Python coverage, exactly as CI measures it.
- The coverage floor **may never be lowered**. A CI step enforces that.
- The front-end thresholds are set to the **current actual** coverage and then held.
- The coverage map is **generated** and CI-verified, not hand-maintained.
- No threshold is introduced that fails on the current `main`. Run the suite first; set the numbers from the output.

## Out of scope

- Raising the coverage floor above the current level — that is a series of separate, focused pull requests.
- Adding tests for the gaps listed in 11.6 — record them, fix them separately.
- Performance or mutation testing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pyproject.toml` has `[tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 90`.
- [ ] The `test` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` passes `--cov-fail-under=90` and fails when the combined coverage is below 90%.
- [ ] The floor does not depend on `CODECOV_TOKEN` and fires on a fork's pull request.
- [ ] `codecov.yml`'s comment states that the authoritative gate is the `test` job.
- [ ] The current `main` passes the new gate — the implementer must run the suite and confirm.
- [ ] A CI step fails if the committed floor is lower than the floor on the base branch.
- [ ] The per-package coverage breakdown is published in the job summary.
- [ ] `apps/studio` has a `test:coverage` script, a v8 coverage provider, and thresholds set to the current actual coverage.
- [ ] The `studio` job uploads front-end coverage, and `codecov.yml` no longer ignores `apps/studio/**`.
- [ ] `scripts/coverage_map.py` generates the coverage map, and a CI step fails on drift against the committed document.
- [ ] The README's coverage map is generated rather than hand-written, and the stale pre-restructure paths are gone.
- [ ] The list of coverage gaps in 11.6 is recorded in the issue or in `docs/architecture/testing.md`.

## Verification

```bash
# The combined number CI sees
uv run pytest --cov=agentic_odi_cli --cov=agentic_odi_connectors --cov=agentic_odi_core \
  --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api --cov-report=term-missing

# The floor fails locally
uv run pytest --cov=agentic_odi_core --cov-fail-under=99   # must fail

# The map is reproducible
uv run python scripts/coverage_map.py --check
```

Add tests:

- `tests/scripts/test_coverage_map.py` — the generator is deterministic; the committed document matches; a test file with no source pair is reported rather than silently dropped.
- A CI smoke step, not a pytest: verify the "floor may not be lowered" check fails when the floor is reduced.

## Context an implementing agent must read

- `pyproject.toml:37-46` — `[tool.coverage.run]`, `testpaths`, and the pytest configuration.
- `codecov.yml` — the current target, the `ignore` list, and `patch.default.informational`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the `test` job, the Codecov upload step and its `fail_ci_if_error: false`, and the `studio` job's `gen:api-types` drift check, which is the pattern the coverage-map drift check should copy.
- `.github/actions/setup/action.yml` — what the shared setup action installs.
- `docs/architecture/testing.md` — where the coverage map belongs.
- `README.md` — the Testing → Test Coverage section, and the hand-maintained Test Coverage Map table.
- `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` and `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` — the repository's existing example of a *generated, contract-tested* artifact; the coverage map should follow the same pattern.
- `apps/studio/package.json` and `apps/studio/vite.config.ts` — the front-end test setup.
- `apps/studio/src/features/flags.test.ts` and `apps/studio/src/ui/UiRenderer.test.tsx` — the front-end test style.
- {{ISSUE_09}} — the guardrails that will reject a diff that lowers the floor.

input.content:
> **TL;DR** — The desktop app reports version `0.1.0` while the project is at `0.12.0`. The release workflow listens for a tag push, but release-please publishes through the API and never sends one — so **no desktop bundle and no signed `latest.json` have ever been published**. The updater therefore has nothing to check for, and the version comparison it makes is against a number that is always wrong. After this issue, the version is one number that moves automatically, the release trigger fires, and the updater manifest is verified in CI before anything is published.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Area** | `area/release` |
| **Priority** | `priority/medium` |
| **Kind** | specification |
| **Depends on** | — |
| **Related PRs** | #76, #15 (closed unmerged) |
| **Blocks** | {{ISSUE_01}} (nothing), but blocks shipping a working desktop app |

---

## The problem

**1. The desktop version is pinned.**
`apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:6` — `"version": "0.1.0"`. `apps/studio/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` and `apps/studio/package.json` carry their own versions. `release-please-config.json` is `release-type: simple` with a single package and **no `extra-files`** — so release-please bumps the root `pyproject.toml` and nothing else.

**Consequence:** every published release ships a desktop app that reports `0.1.0`. The updater's version comparison is meaningless, and the "Update ready" indicator can never be right.

**2. The release workflow never fires.**
`.github/workflows/release.yml:6-8` and `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml:6-9` trigger on `push: tags: v*`. release-please publishes through the GitHub API (`release-please-action`), which **does not emit a `push: tags` event**.

**Consequence:** for every release cut so far (0.7.0 → 0.12.0), the tag was created without a tag-push event, so `release.yml` and `tauri-release.yml` never ran. **No desktop bundle, no `latest.json`, and no signed updater artifact has ever been published.** The updater feature in `apps/studio/src/components/updater/useUpdater.ts` has been polling for a file that does not exist.

**3. The updater end-to-end test is manual only.**
PR #76 adds `scripts/verify-desktop-update.sh` — a real E2E that builds two signed AppImages with a throwaway key, serves a local `latest.json`, runs 0.1.0, and watches it replace its own file. It is **not wired into CI**. The in-place relaunch path is covered only by unit tests over an injected transport.

**4. The version check has a hole.**
Nothing verifies that the published `latest.json` advertises the tag's version and carries signed artifacts for every platform. A release can publish a broken updater manifest and nobody finds out until a user tries to update.

**5. The release still needs a human.**
The release-please workflow arms auto-merge on the release PR and `main` requires the `CI green` check, so the release PR merges itself once CI is green. But:
- the `main-requires-ci-green` ruleset has an admin bypass with `bypass_mode: "always"` and `strict_required_status_checks_policy: false`;
- the `RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID` / `RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets may not be configured, in which case the workflow falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which cannot start a tag-push workflow;
- the repository has accumulated **~50 unmerged remote branches**, and `release-please-config.json` has `delete_branch_on_merge: false`.

**6. Six releases in one day.**
0.7.0 → 0.12.0 in a single day, each a release PR of +8…+22 lines, each hand-merged within minutes. That is not a pipeline; it is a person clicking.

## What a person experiences

A developer lands a fix. Within an hour, a new version is published, the desktop app's version number has moved, the `latest.json` manifest is signed and present, and the CI log says *"verified: latest.json advertises 0.13.0 and carries signed artifacts for linux-x86_64, windows-x86_64, darwin-aarch64, darwin-x86_64"*. A person with the app installed sees a quiet bar above the conversation four seconds after launch, downloads in the background, and applies the update on the next ordinary launch — without them having to know any of this happened. And if any of it is broken, the release fails loudly instead of shipping a broken updater to a user.

## Specification

### 12.1 One version, moved automatically

- `release-please-config.json` — add `extra-files`:

```json
"extra-files": [
  "apps/studio/package.json",
  "apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json",
  "apps/studio/src-tauri/Cargo.toml"
]
```

- Verify each of the three actually holds a `version` field that release-please can update:
  - `apps/studio/package.json` — `"version"`.
  - `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` — `"version"` (this is the Tauri build version).
  - `apps/studio/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` — `[[package]] version = "…"`.
  - `apps/studio/src-tauri/Cargo.lock` is regenerated by cargo, not edited.
- **Also bump the three files to the current release version (`0.12.0`) in the same pull request**, so the next release starts from the truth rather than from `0.1.0`. This is the fix that unblocks the updater immediately.
- `packages/core/pyproject.toml`, `packages/connectors/pyproject.toml`, `apps/*/pyproject.toml` — check whether each carries its own `version`. If they do, they need `extra-files` entries too, or a documented decision that only the root and the studio are versioned.
- **Add a test** that asserts the version in `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, `apps/studio/package.json`, `apps/studio/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, and the root `pyproject.toml` are **all equal**. A drift here is exactly the bug.

### 12.2 The release trigger that actually fires

- `.github/workflows/release.yml` and `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml` — add:

```yaml
on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
```

`release: published` is the event release-please actually produces. `push: tags` stays for hand-cut tags.

- **Make the trigger a test.** Add a CI check that asserts both workflows list `release: types: [published]`. A workflow that silently stops listening is invisible otherwise.

### 12.3 Verify the updater manifest before publishing

PR #76 adds a `verify` job to `tauri-release.yml` that fails the release if `latest.json` is absent, advertises the wrong version, or lacks signed artifacts for `linux-x86_64`, `windows-x86_64`, `darwin-aarch64`, `darwin-x86_64`. **That job must be part of this issue** — the release is only trustworthy if the manifest is checked.

- The verify job must:
  - download the published `latest.json`;
  - assert `version` equals the tag's version;
  - assert every expected platform key is present;
  - assert each referenced artifact URL resolves (HTTP 200) and its `.sig` exists;
  - assert the artifacts are attached to the GitHub Release, not merely present in the job's artifacts.
- **The `verify` job must run before the release is considered successful** and must fail the workflow on a mismatch.

### 12.4 The updater E2E in CI

- `scripts/verify-desktop-update.sh` (from PR #76) — wire it into `.github/workflows/tauri-release.yml` as a job, or into `ci.yml` on a schedule.
- It needs a Linux display for the AppImage path. The job must install `xvfb` and run under `xvfb-run`, or the script must be made headless-safe.
- It builds two signed AppImages with a throwaway minisign key, so the job needs **no repository secret** — the key is generated in-job. It must never touch `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`.
- If the E2E cannot be made reliable in CI, it must still run **weekly on a schedule** so a broken updater is caught within days, and the issue must say which.

### 12.5 The release pipeline, fully autonomous

- **Configure the GitHub App secrets.** `RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_CLIENT_ID` and `RELEASE_PLEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` must exist as repository secrets, or the workflow must fall back in a way that still triggers the tag workflow. The README documents this setup (see the "One-time setup (GitHub App)" section) but nothing verifies it is done. **Add a CI check that asserts the secrets exist** (`gh secret list` in a workflow with `secrets: read`, or a manual check recorded in the issue).
- **Tighten the ruleset.** `strict_required_status_checks_policy: true`, and the admin bypass changed from `always`. {{ISSUE_09}} owns this.
- **Branch hygiene.** `release-please-config.json` — set `"delete_branch_on_merge": true`. Then run a one-time cleanup of the ~50 stale remote branches. **Do not delete a branch that has an open pull request.**
- **The `CI green` aggregator must include the release-critical jobs.** Today `ci-green` needs `lint, typecheck, security, test, smoke, website, studio, tauri-check, tauri-build`. The version-parity check and the workflow-trigger check from 12.1 and 12.2 must be added to it.

### 12.6 The version must be visible to the person

- `apps/studio/src/components/layout/StudioBar.tsx` — the running version must be shown. PR #76 puts it there behind the updater work; this issue requires it regardless of the updater's state, because a person must be able to tell which build they are running.
- `apps/studio/src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx` — a **Settings → About** section with the version, the build date, the platform, and the update status. The updater's "Check now / Skip this version / auto-check toggle" (PR #76) lives there.
- The CLI already prints a version: `python -m agentic_odi --version`. Verify it reports the **released** version, not a hardcoded string. `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/version.py` and `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/_build_info.py` are the files to check.

## Non-negotiable constraints

- **One version number.** The root, the studio package, the Tauri config, and the Rust crate must agree, and a test must enforce it.
- The release trigger must include `release: types: [published]`. A tag-only trigger does not fire.
- The `verify` job must run and must fail the release on a manifest mismatch. A verification step that only warns is not a verification step.
- The updater E2E must not require a repository secret.
- The E2E must never use `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`.
- The `verify` job must check the artifacts **attached to the Release**, not just the ones produced in the job.

## Out of scope

- The updater's own design — PR #76 owns the reducer, the service, the transport, and the platform rules.
- The `tauri-plugin-process` capability grant — PR #76 owns it.
- Notarization and Apple Developer ID signing — configured by the existing secrets, verified here only insofar as the `verify` job checks the artifacts exist.
- A `latest.json` for the CLI binary distribution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `release-please-config.json` lists `extra-files` for `apps/studio/package.json`, `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, and `apps/studio/src-tauri/Cargo.toml`.

input.content:
> **TL;DR** — The Studio's sidecar has no authentication, the MCP server has no authentication, the desktop app ships with content-security-policy set to `null`, and the Cloudflare Worker tunnels the sidecar to a public URL. Anyone who finds that URL can read your ODI store, write to it, and drive the LLM with your API key. The connector registry already does the credential handling correctly — `${VAR}` placeholders resolved from the environment — so the pattern exists; it just was not applied to the rest. After this issue, the hosted Studio and the local sidecar have a real front door.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Area** | `area/studio`, `area/core` |
| **Priority** | `priority/high` |
| **Kind** | specification |
| **Depends on** | {{ISSUE_04}} (the API key must move server-side first) |
| **Related PRs** | — |
| **Blocks** | {{ISSUE_18}} (a background agent needs an authenticated, scoped identity) |

---

## The problem

**1. The sidecar has no authentication at all.**
`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/app.py:19-31` — a hardcoded `CORS_ORIGINS` allowlist, and no auth middleware, no API key, no session, nothing. Every route is open:

- `POST /api/chat` — spends the person's LLM tokens and can call every MCP tool.
- `GET /api/canvas` — reads the entire ODI store.
- `POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/jobs`, `/api/steps`, `/api/outcomes` — writes and deletes.
- `GET /api/config` — returns the LLM base URL and model.
- `POST /api/connectors` — registers connectors.

`docs/architecture/data-flow.md` states the position honestly: *"MCP is an HTTP service with no authentication in local development. Do not expose it directly to the internet."* But the sidecar **is** exposed to the internet.

**2. The Cloudflare Worker tunnels the sidecar to a public URL.**
`infra/cloudflare/worker.ts` and `wrangler.jsonc` — the hosted Studio at `https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/` proxies to the sidecar. The README calls it "the experimental Living Studio UI" and links to it as the project's front door. If the Worker forwards `/api/*` to the sidecar, then the sidecar's unauthenticated surface is on the public internet, and it is a **write** surface, not just a read one.

**3. The MCP server has no authentication either.**
`apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:478-479` — `mcp.run(transport="http", port=8000)`. The README's Deployment section says authentication is required for the hosted MCP endpoint at `https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp` — that is the *hosted* platform, not this server. A locally-bound MCP server that binds `0.0.0.0` is reachable from the LAN.

**4. The desktop app's CSP is `null`.**
`apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:24-26` — `"csp": null`. The webview renders **model-authored Markdown** and **model-authored UI specs**. `apps/studio/src/components/chat/Markdown.tsx` and `apps/studio/src/ui/UiRenderer.tsx` are the two parsers. The UI protocol is defensively built — `apps/studio/src/ui/protocol.ts` strips unknown props, bounds depth and node count, and the renderer has a per-node error boundary — but that is a **rendering** defense, not a **scripting** defense. With no CSP, an XSS in the Markdown path has the whole webview.

**5. The API key lives in `localStorage`.**
`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:435-442` — the LLM API key is stored in the browser's `localStorage` under `studio.settings`. Any XSS in the webview, any shared machine, and any browser extension with storage access can read it. The Settings panel also displays it in a text input.

**6. The connector registry is the one place that got it right — and it shows the pattern.**
`packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/catalog.py:66-71` and `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/registry.py` — presets store `${VAR}` placeholders; `MCPClientConnector.transport()` (`packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/mcp/connector.py:74-88`) resolves them from the environment at connection time and raises `MissingEnvironmentError` for anything absent. **Credentials never enter the registry.** The README says so explicitly: *"Credentials never enter the registry."* That is the correct design and it should be the template for the rest.

**7. No request identity.**
Nothing in the request path carries an actor, a session, or a request id. {{ISSUE_05}} needs a `decided_by`; {{ISSUE_14}} needs a `request_id`; {{ISSUE_18}} needs a per-agent identity. All three are blocked on there being an identity to attribute an action to.

## What a person experiences

You install the desktop app. It starts the sidecar on `127.0.0.1:8100` and generates a **random per-install access token**, stored in `~/.config/agentic-odi/` with mode `0600`. The webview receives it over the Tauri bridge and sends it as a bearer token. The token is checked on every `/api/*` request; a request without it is refused. On a shared machine, opening the Studio asks for the token once and remembers it for the session. On the hosted Studio, a person reaches the URL and is asked for an access code before anything renders. Your LLM key is never in the browser: the sidecar holds it, the browser sees a masked value, and the API key never crosses the wire. The Tauri webview runs under a content-security-policy that permits the app's own assets and nothing else.

## Specification

### 13.1 A local access token

- `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/` — add a small module for the token: `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/access.py`.
  - `load_or_create_token() -> str` — reads `~/.config/agentic-odi/access-token`, or creates one with `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, writes it with mode `0600`, and creates the directory with mode `0700`.
  - `verify_token(provided: str | None) -> bool` — a **constant-time** comparison (`hmac.compare_digest`).
  - `AGENTIC_ODI_ACCESS_TOKEN` overrides the file, for CI and for tests.
- `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/app.py` — add a dependency or middleware that checks `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (or an `X-Access-Token` header) on every `/api/*` route, **except**:
  - `GET /health` — the liveness probe, so a health check does not need a credential. It must return only `{"status": "ok"}` and nothing else.
  - the static SPA assets and the SPA fallback — the shell must load so the app can show its "enter your access code" screen.
  - `POST /api/auth` — the exchange endpoint (13.2).
- **A browser build cannot have a bearer header on a static asset request**, so the SPA must fetch the token through a bridge:
  - **Tauri**: `apps/studio/src/bridge/desktopBridge.ts` — add an async `getAccessToken()` that calls a Tauri command. `apps/studio/src-tauri/src/lib.rs` — add `#[tauri::command] async fn access_token() -> String` that reads the token file directly and returns it. **The command must be registered and the capability in `src-tauri/capabilities/default.json` must permit it.** The token is exposed to the webview — that is unavoidable, since the webview must call the sidecar — but it is never persisted to `localStorage` and never written to a log.
  - **Browser (Vite dev / the hosted Worker)**: the person is prompted for an access code. `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx` — add an unauthenticated state that shows a single input, and a `POST /api/auth` call that exchanges the code for a **short-lived session token** (an HMAC-signed value with an expiry, not the long-lived access token).
- `apps/studio/src/api/studioApi.ts` — attach the token to every request.

### 13.2 The hosted Studio

- `infra/cloudflare/worker.ts` — the Worker must **not** proxy `/api/*` to the sidecar without a check.
  - Require a valid session token on every `/api/*` request before proxying.
  - Serve the SPA shell unconditionally so the sign-in screen can load.
- The access code is configured by `AGENTIC_ODI_ACCESS_CODE` (or the `ACCESS_CODE` Worker secret) and is compared with `hmac.compare_digest`.
- **The Worker must not log the token or the code.** `wrangler.jsonc` — add the required secret names to the documentation.
- The README's Deployment section must state plainly: *"The hosted Studio requires an access code. It is a single shared secret and it is not a multi-user system."* The project's own scope should be honest about this.

### 13.3 The MCP server

- `apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:478-479` — bind to `127.0.0.1` by default, not `0.0.0.0`. Add a `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_HOST` override for the deliberate case where a LAN binding is wanted.
- Add bearer-token verification to the MCP HTTP transport, using the same `agentic_odi_core.access` module. A shared secret is enough for a local tool server; document that MCP's own auth model is the right answer for a multi-tenant deployment.
- `docs/architecture/data-flow.md` — update the "Trust Boundaries" section to state what is now enforced.

### 13.4 The API key leaves the browser

- `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:435-442` — the API key must **not** be stored in `localStorage` and must not be returned to the browser.
- Add a `Settings` entity in the store, persisted server-side, holding the LLM base URL, model, API key, and MCP URL. The API key is write-only from the browser's perspective:
  - `PUT /api/settings` accepts the key and stores it.
  - `GET /api/settings` returns everything **except** the key, plus `{"has_api_key": true, "api_key_hint": "sk-…4f2a"}` — the first three and the last four characters only.
- The key is stored in `~/.config/agentic-odi/settings.json` with the file mode `0600`.
- The Settings panel's API key field becomes a write-only field: it shows the hint, and saving replaces the value. It never renders the stored key.
- **This is the part that makes the hosted Studio safe**: the key stays on the machine that owns it.

### 13.5 A Content Security Policy for the desktop app

- `apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:24-26` — replace `"csp": null` with a real policy:

```
"default-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: asset: http://asset.localhost; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' http://127.0.0.1:8100 ipc: http://ipc.localhost; font-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'"
```

- **Why `'unsafe-inline'` for styles and not for scripts.** The app uses inline styles in several components; removing that is a separate, larger task. Scripts get no exception. Note the policy in the PR body with the reason.
- `connect-src` must include `http://127.0.0.1:8100` (the sidecar) and the Tauri IPC origins. If the app ever needs a remote LLM base URL, that is a **user-configured** origin, and the policy must not become `connect-src *` to accommodate it — the WebView's own fetch to the LLM is not used (the sidecar does the LLM call), so `connect-src` stays tight.
- Verify the Markdown renderer cannot execute script: `apps/studio/src/components/chat/Markdown.tsx` — it must not use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with unsanitized content, or it must use a sanitizer. Whichever it is, the CSP is the backstop; the sanitizer is the front line. **Both must be in place.**
- `apps/studio/src/ui/UiRenderer.tsx` — the UI protocol renders React components, not HTML, so it is already safe. Confirm and note it.

### 13.6 A request identity, for everything downstream

- Add a `request_id` to every `/api/*` request, generated at the edge (the middleware) and propagated into:
  - the sidecar's log lines (see {{ISSUE_14}});
  - the MCP tool call, as a header, so the MCP server's log lines share it;
  - the `Execution` record (see {{ISSUE_05}});
  - the SSE events for that request.
- The MCP server logs the same `request_id`.
- The `request_id` is **not** a credential and must not be used as one.

### 13.7 Audit the rest of the secret surface

- `scripts/`, `.github/workflows/`, and `packaging/pyinstaller/odi.spec` — grep for hardcoded secrets, tokens, and keys. The repository's `.gitignore` and `git log` must be checked for a committed `living-studio.key` (the README documents moving it out of the repo at `~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/`; confirm it was never committed).
- `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/paths.py` — every file the CLI writes that may contain a secret must be created with mode `0600`: `~/.config/agentic-odi/settings.json`, `llm_profile.json`, `connectors.json`, and the access token.
- `bandit` is already in CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the `security` job) over `apps` and `packages`. **Extend it to cover the new access and settings modules** and add `B105`/`B106` (hardcoded password string) to the selected checks if they are not already selected.

## Non-negotiable constraints

- **Every `/api/*` route requires a credential**, except `GET /health` (which returns only `{"status": "ok"}`) and the static SPA assets.
- Token comparison is **constant-time**.
- The access token file is mode `0600`; its directory is `0700`.
- The **LLM API key never leaves the server side**. The browser receives a hint, never the value, and never stores it in `localStorage`.
- The Tauri webview's CSP is not `null` and `script-src` has no `'unsafe-inline'` and no `'unsafe-eval'`.
- The MCP server binds to `127.0.0.1` by default.
- Credentials are never logged, and the connector pattern (`${VAR}` placeholders resolved at use) is the model — no credential is ever written to a registry or a settings file that is read by a browser.
- The hosted Studio requires an access code, and the README says so.

## Out of scope

- Multi-user accounts, per-user identities, or a role model. The product is a single-user local tool with a shared hosted demo.
- Replacing FastMCP's own authentication with a full OAuth flow — a shared bearer token is proportionate for a local tool server, and the issue says so.
- Secret rotation tooling for the hosted access code. Document the manual rotation instead.
- End-to-end encryption between the browser and the sidecar — it is a loopback socket, and the hosted path is TLS at the Worker.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `agentic_odi_core.access` provides `load_or_create_token` and `verify_token`, with constant-time comparison.
- [ ] The access token file is created with mode `0600` inside a `0700` directory; `AGENTIC_ODI_ACCESS_TOKEN` overrides it.
- [ ] Every `/api/*` route except `GET /health` and the static assets requires a valid credential; `GET /health` returns only `{"status": "ok"}`.
- [ ] The Tauri build obtains the token through a Tauri command and the capability file permits it; the token is never written to `localStorage`.
- [ ] The browser build prompts for an access code and exchanges it for a short-lived session token; the long-lived token is never sent to a browser.
- [ ] The Worker requires a session token on every `/api/*` request and serves the SPA shell unconditionally.
- [ ] The README's Deployment section states that the hosted Studio requires an access code and is not a multi-user system.
- [ ] The MCP server binds to `127.0.0.1` by default and verifies a bearer token.
- [ ] The LLM API key is stored server-side with mode `0600`; `GET /api/settings` returns a hint, never the value; the SPA never stores the key in `localStorage`.
- [ ] `tauri.conf.json` has a real CSP with `script-src 'self'` and no `'unsafe-inline'` or `'unsafe-eval'` in `script-src`.
- [ ] The Markdown renderer does not execute unsanitized HTML.
- [ ] Every request carries a `request_id` that appears in the sidecar log line, the MCP server log line, the `Execution` record, and the SSE events.
- [ ] Every file the CLI writes that may hold a secret is created with mode `0600`.
- [ ] A secret scan finds no committed key; `living-studio.key` was never in the repository.
- [ ] Bandit covers the new modules and the relevant checks are enabled.

## Verification

```bash
# The sidecar refuses an unauthenticated write
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/jobs \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"nope"}'      # expect 401

# Health stays open and says nothing
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8100/health                            # expect {"status":"ok"}

# With the token
TOKEN=$(cat ~/.config/agentic-odi/access-token)
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/jobs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"ok"}'  # expect 2xx

# File modes
stat -c '%a %n' ~/.config/agentic-odi ~/.config/agentic-odi/access-token ~/.config/agentic-odi/settings.json

# Secret scan
git log --all --full-history -- '**/living-studio.key' '**/*.pem' '**/*.key' | head
```

Add tests:

- `packages/core/tests/test_access.py` — token creation, mode `0600`, constant-time verification, the env override.
- `apps/studio-api/tests/test_auth.py` — every route is protected; `/health` is open and minimal; a wrong token is 401; the token in the query string is not accepted.
- `apps/studio-api/tests/test_settings_secret.py` — `GET /api/settings` never contains the key; `PUT` stores it; the file mode is `0600`.
- `apps/studio/src/api/studioApi.test.ts` — the token is attached to every request and is not persisted to `localStorage`.

input.content:
> **TL;DR** — The Studio fails in a lot of ways and says almost nothing about any of them. If the MCP server is down mid-answer, the stream just stops. If the sidecar forwards a tool call that failed, the API answers `{"ok": true, "result": "Error: Job with ID … not found"}` — success, with the error inside. If a connector fails to register, the error event is dropped on the floor and the person sees nothing. If the canvas fails to load, the screen says "No opportunities match the current filter criteria", which is a lie about a broken connection. After this issue, every failure has a face, a cause, and a next step.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Area** | `area/studio` |
| **Priority** | `priority/high` |
| **Kind** | specification |
| **Depends on** | — |
| **Related PRs** | — |
| **Blocks** | {{ISSUE_14}} is a prerequisite for {{ISSUE_13}}? No — {{ISSUE_13}} owns request ids; this issue consumes them. |

---

## The problem

**1. The sidecar reports failures as successes.**
`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/router.py:146-157` (jobs), `:191-205` (steps), `:239-263` (outcomes), `:266-280` (patch outcome) — each calls `call_mcp_tool` and unconditionally returns `{"ok": True, "result": <string>}`.

The MCP server returns failures as **strings**, not exceptions (`apps/mcp-server/src/agentic_odi_mcp_server/mcp_server.py:114` — `"Error: Job with ID … not found."`, `:118` — `"Error: importance and satisfaction must be between 1.0 and 10.0"`). So the sidecar wraps an error message in `ok: true` and hands it to the SPA as a success.

**The CLI already solves this.** `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/backend.py:545-559` — `_parse_remote` raises `BackendError` if the text starts with `"Error:"` or contains `" not found:"`. The sidecar does not. The same repo, two answers.

**2. The chat stream dies without an event.**
`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:259-276`:
- `mcp_client.list_tools()` at `:259-260` is not wrapped in `try/except`. If the MCP server is down, the `async with McpClient(...)` raises **after** `status: mcp_tools` has already been streamed. The SSE stream dies mid-flight with no `error` event.
- The LLM completion call at `:270` is not wrapped either.
- The MCP server is **never health-checked in the chat path** — only the LLM is (`chat.py:239-240` → `probes.check_llm_health`). The agent can announce "I found the tools" and then fail on the first one.

**3. The connector error event is dropped by the client.**
The sidecar emits `{"status": "error", "error": ...}` (`chat.py:182`). The client reads only `event.data.preset ?? event.data.name` (`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:768-770`) — **both are absent on the error path**, so the id is `""` and the event is discarded. **A failed connector registration is completely invisible to the person.**

**4. The connector list goes stale.**
`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:767-775` — the `connector` event does not call `refreshConnectors()`. The list only refreshes when the person dismisses the suggestion chip (`Composer.tsx:157`) or at boot (`:862`). Settings can show a stale list indefinitely.

**5. A canvas failure is dressed as an empty result.**
`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:515-531` — on error, `canvasLoading` is false and `canvas` stays null. The render condition is `canvasLoading && !canvas`, so the skeleton never shows, and `OpportunityLandscape` renders a metrics grid of zeros plus *"No opportunities match the current filter criteria."* (`apps/studio/src/components/canvas/OpportunityLandscape.tsx:101-102,161-187`). **An error is shown as an empty result.**

**6. The skeleton is unreachable on a warm start.**
`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:270` — the canvas is restored from `localStorage` at init, so `canvas` is non-null, so `canvasLoading && !canvas` is false and the skeleton never appears. The person sees stale data during a refresh with no indication that a refresh is happening.

**7. The assistant can fail with no reply at all.**
`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:798-816` — if the stream errors before any content, `sendMessage` pops the empty assistant message and the person is left with their own message and no answer — only a toast, which auto-dismisses after 6 s (`:343-345`).

**8. Silent error swallowing in the client.**
`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:364-370` — the connector catalog fetch error is swallowed. `SettingsPanel` renders an empty `<select>` with no explanation (`:151-200`).

**9. `DirectCapture` has no inline error state.**
`apps/studio/src/components/canvas/DirectCapture.tsx:47-64` — a failed submit clears nothing and shows only a toast.

**10. The workspace lens has no error boundary.**
`apps/studio/src/components/workspace/WorkspacePanel.tsx:72-74` — a throw inside a panel bubbles to the app-level `ErrorBoundary` (`apps/studio/src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx:22-37`), which offers only *"Reload the studio"* — losing the whole session. The per-node `NodeBoundary` (`apps/studio/src/ui/UiRenderer.tsx:53-64`) protects agent-composed surfaces but not the panels.

**11. The tool-round cap truncates silently.**
`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:26` — `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 3`. When the loop exits because of the cap, it emits a `message` with the accumulated prose (`:373`) and the model never gets to answer after its third tool call. The person sees no explanation.

**12. Two routes skip the MCP URL guard.**
`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/router.py:196` and `:244` — `POST /api/steps` and `POST /api/outcomes` pass `body.mcp_url` straight to `call_mcp_tool`, while every other route uses `_require_mcp_url` (`:55-58`, `:166`, `:213`, `:271`). An empty URL yields a confusing 502 instead of a 400.

**13. Health is probed once and never again.**
`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:864-881` — the bar shows "Local mode" forever if the model comes up later. Only the wizard's readiness step re-probes (`apps/studio/src/onboarding/FirstRunWizard.tsx:57-71`).

## What a person experiences

You ask the agent a question. The MCP server is not running. Instead of the answer simply stopping, the conversation shows, in place, a small panel: *"I could not reach the ODI server at http://localhost:8000/mcp. Your question was saved. Start the server and try again."* — with a **Retry** button that re-runs the turn. If the sidecar cannot reach the LLM, the same panel says *"The model at http://localhost:8001/v1 is not responding."* and offers to switch to the local model. If a save fails because the outcome is malformed, the form says exactly which field is wrong and shows the fix. **Nothing fails quietly, and nothing is dressed up as success.**

## Specification

### 14.1 A single error vocabulary

Create `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/errors.py`:

```python
class StudioErrorCode(StrEnum):
    MCP_UNREACHABLE = "mcp_unreachable"
    MCP_TOOL_FAILED = "mcp_tool_failed"
    LLM_UNREACHABLE = "llm_unreachable"
    LLM_TOOL_ROUNDS_EXHAUSTED = "llm_tool_rounds_exhausted"
    NOT_FOUND = "not_found"
    VALIDATION = "validation"
    OUT_OF_RANGE = "out_of_range"
    CONFLICT = "conflict"
    INTERNAL = "internal"

class StudioError(BaseModel):
    code: StudioErrorCode
    message: str            # plain language, addressed to the person
    detail: str | None = None      # the technical text, for a disclosure
    suggestion: str | None = None  # the next step
    retryable: bool = False
    request_id: str | None = None
```

- The MCP server's string-error convention is preserved at the tool boundary. The sidecar **parses** the string and converts it into a `StudioError` with a code, a suggestion, and a `retryable` flag.
- The parser replaces the CLI's ad-hoc sniffing (`backend.py:545-559`) and is shared by the sidecar and the CLI. **Move it into `packages/core` so both use one implementation** — `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/remote.py::parse_tool_result(text) -> StudioError | None`.
- Every HTTP error response in the sidecar uses the same body shape, so the SPA has **one** error path.

### 14.2 The sidecar must not report errors as successes

- `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/router.py:146-157`, `:191-205`, `:239-263`, `:266-280` — when `call_mcp_tool` returns a string that parses as an error, the route must return the appropriate HTTP status with the `StudioError` body:
  - `not found` → `404`
  - `out of range` / `validation` → `422`
  - `mcp_unreachable` → `502` with `retryable: true`
  - otherwise → `500`
- `{"ok": true}` is removed from these responses. The response **is** the result.
- `POST /api/steps` and `POST /api/outcomes` (`:196`, `:244`) must call `_require_mcp_url` like every other route, so an empty URL is a `400`, not a confusing `502`.

### 14.3 The chat stream must never die silently

`apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/chat.py:235-373`:

- **Health-check the MCP server before advertising its tools.** Probe it alongside the LLM at `:239-240`. If it is unreachable, emit `status: "mcp_unreachable"` and return a `message` that says so — do not open the client, do not list tools, do not pretend.
- **Wrap every step of the loop in `try/except`:**
  - the `McpClient` construction and `list_tools()` (`:259-260`);
  - the LLM completion call (`:270`);
  - each `call_tool` (`:313-367`).
- **A fatal error emits an `error` SSE event** before the stream closes, with the `StudioError` body. The stream must always end with either a `message` or an `error` — never both, never neither.
- **The tool-round cap must be explained.** When the loop exits because of `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS`, the sidecar emits a `message` that includes: *"I reached the limit of 3 tool rounds for this turn. Here is what I have so far — ask me to continue and I will pick up from here."* A cap that truncates without saying so is a lie by omission.
- A tool error that the model can recover from stays a tool result (the current behavior at `:354-358` is right) — but the error is also recorded in the turn's log with the `request_id`.

### 14.4 The client must show failures, and must not drop them

`apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:717-782` — the SSE dispatcher:

- **Handle the `error` event.** Currently `apps/studio/src/api/sse.ts:10-46` synthesizes an `error` event on malformed JSON, but the sidecar never sends one. Add a real `error` handler that renders an inline failure panel in the transcript — not a toast, because a toast auto-dismisses (`:343-345`) and the failure is the last thing the person needs to see.
- **Handle the connector error event.** `StudioContext.tsx:767-775` — read `event.data.error` when `event.data.status === "error"` and surface it. Today it is dropped because the handler only reads `preset` and `name`.
- **Call `refreshConnectors()` after any connector event**, so the list is never stale.
- **Do not pop the assistant message when the stream fails.** `:798-816` — keep a failed assistant turn in the transcript with the failure panel, and keep the person's question. A failure that erases the conversation is the worst possible failure.
- **Re-probe health periodically.** Add a poll — every 30 s while the window is focused, and on `visibilitychange` — that calls `POST /api/health/mcp` and `POST /api/health/llm`. The top bar's status must be able to change from "Local mode" to "Connected" without a reload.

### 14.5 Distinct empty states, and no error-as-empty

The rule: **an empty result and a failure are different, and the interface must never show one when the other is true.**

- `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:515-531` — the canvas state must be a discriminated union, not four loose booleans:
  ```ts
  type CanvasState =
    | { kind: "loading" }
    | { kind: "ready"; data: CanvasData }
    | { kind: "empty"; data: CanvasData }
    | { kind: "error"; error: StudioError };
  ```
  - `loading` → the skeleton (`apps/studio/src/components/Skeletons.tsx`).
  - `ready` → the content.
  - `empty` → *"No opportunities yet. Tell me the job your customers are trying to get done."* — the empty state must be **an invitation**, not a zero-filled metrics grid.
  - `error` → the failure panel with a **Retry** button.
- `apps/studio/src/components/canvas/OpportunityLandscape.tsx:101-102,161-187` — the zero-filled metrics grid must only render for a genuinely empty result, never for an error.
- **The skeleton must appear on a refresh**, even with a warm cache. The current condition `canvasLoading && !canvas` (`:515`) is wrong; use the union.
- `apps/studio/src/components/workspace/panels.tsx:34-98` and `WorkspacePanel.tsx:72-74` — every lens gets its own error boundary, so a throw in one panel shows a panel-level failure with a Retry, not a whole-app "Reload the studio" that destroys the session.

### 14.6 Forms must show their errors in place

- `apps/studio/src/components/canvas/DirectCapture.tsx:47-64` — add an inline error state per field, driven by the `422` body from the sidecar. The `suggestion` from the server is shown next to the field.
- `apps/studio/src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:151-200` — a failed catalog fetch renders an explicit error with a Retry, not an empty `<select>`.
- `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.tsx:364-370` — stop swallowing the error; surface it.

### 14.7 One request id, one log line, one trail

- Generate a `request_id` per chat turn and per API request, at the edge.
- Log **one structured line per turn**, at the end:
  ```json
  {"ts": "…", "level": "info", "event": "chat_turn", "request_id": "…",
   "model": "local-tools-model", "rounds": 2, "tool_calls": 3,
   "tool_errors": 1, "duration_ms": 1840, "outcome": "completed"}
  ```
  `outcome` is `completed`, `failed`, `partial`, or `rounds_exhausted`.
- The same `request_id` must appear in the MCP server's log line, in the `Execution` record ({{ISSUE_05}}), and in the SSE events for that turn.
- **Never log the token, the API key, or the contents of a tool result that may contain customer data.** Redact by key name at the logger boundary, and test it.

## Non-negotiable constraints

- **Every failure reaches the person.** There is no path where the app fails and the person is not told.
- **An error is never rendered as an empty result, and never rendered as success.**
- Every stream ends with exactly one of `message` or `error`.
- The `request_id` is present on every log line, on every SSE event, and on every `Execution`.
- No secret and no customer data is written to a log line.
- The sidecar and the CLI share one tool-result parser.
- The failure panel offers a **Retry** that re-runs the turn, not only a description.

## Out of scope

- Authentication — {{ISSUE_13}}.
- The audit trail — {{ISSUE_05}}.
- Structured logging as a general observability system; this issue introduces the minimum needed to make failures diagnosable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `StudioError` and `StudioErrorCode` exist in `apps/studio-api/src/agentic_odi_studio_api/studio/errors.py`, and every HTTP error uses that shape.
- [ ] The tool-result parser lives in `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/remote.py` and is used by both the sidecar and the CLI.
- [ ] The sidecar no longer returns `{"ok": true}` around a tool error; the routes return 404 / 422 / 502 / 500 as appropriate.
- [ ] `POST /api/steps` and `POST /api/outcomes` use `_require_mcp_url` and return 400 on an empty URL.
- [ ] The chat path health-checks the MCP server before advertising its tools.
- [ ] The `McpClient` construction, `list_tools()`, the LLM completion call, and each `call_tool` are all wrapped; a fatal error emits an `error` SSE event.
- [ ] Every stream ends with exactly one of `message` or `error`.
- [ ] Hitting `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` produces a message that says the limit was reached.
- [ ] The client handles the `error` event and the connector error event, and neither is dropped.
- [ ] `refreshConnectors()` runs after any connector event.
- [ ] A failed stream keeps the person's question and shows a failure panel with a Retry; the assistant message is not popped.
- [ ] Health is re-probed on an interval and on window focus, and the top bar status can change without a reload.
- [ ] The canvas state is a discriminated union with `loading` / `ready` / `empty` / `error`; an error never renders the zero-filled metrics grid.
- [ ] The skeleton appears during a warm refresh.
- [ ] Every lens has its own error boundary with a Retry; a panel throw never reaches the app-level boundary.
- [ ] `DirectCapture` and `SettingsPanel` show their errors in place, with the server's suggestion.
- [ ] One structured log line per chat turn, with the `request_id`, the tool count, the error count, the duration, and the outcome.
- [ ] A redaction test proves that a token, an API key, and a customer quote are not written to the log.

## Verification

```bash
uv run --directory apps/studio-api pytest
uv run --directory apps/cli pytest
uv run --directory packages/core pytest
npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run
npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck && npm --prefix apps/studio run lint
uv run --directory apps/studio-api mypy .
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .

# Manual
# 1. Stop the MCP server, ask a question, observe the failure panel and the error event.
# 2. Send a malformed outcome and observe the 422 with the suggestion.
```

Add tests:

- `packages/core/tests/test_remote.py` — the parser classifies every error string shape; a success string is not misclassified.
- `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_errors.py` — the route status mapping; the shared error body shape.
- `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_chat_branches.py` — extend: MCP unreachable, the LLM raising, the round cap exhausted, and the "exactly one of message or error" invariant.
- `apps/studio/src/state/StudioContext.test.tsx` (new) — the `error` event renders a panel; the connector error event is surfaced; `refreshConnectors` runs; a failed stream keeps the question.
- `apps/studio/src/components/canvas/OpportunityLandscape.test.tsx` (new) — `error` does not render the zero grid; `empty` renders the invitation.
- `apps/studio/src/components/workspace/WorkspacePanel.test.tsx` — a throwing panel shows the panel-level error, not the app boundary.
- `apps/studio/src/components/canvas/DirectCapture.test.tsx` (new) — an inline field error with the server's suggestion.

> **TL;DR** — The Studio's flagship visual is an interactive map of opportunities drawn as an SVG. To a screen reader it is a blank rectangle, and to a keyboard it is a wall. The same is true of the landscape table rows, the job-map tiles, and every notification card. There is one mobile pull request open that claims to fix touch targets — and it targets a shell that no longer exists. After this issue, every person can drive the Studio without a mouse, and the accessibility claims are verified in CI rather than asserted.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Area** | `area/studio` |
| **Priority** | `priority/medium` |
| **Kind** | specification |
| **Depends on** | — |
| **Related PRs** | #66 |
| **Blocks** | {{ISSUE_16}} |

---

## The problem

**1. The opportunity matrix is unusable without a mouse.**
`apps/studio/src/components/canvas/OpportunityLandscape.tsx:227-355` — the `<svg>` has no `role="img"`, no `<title>`, no `<desc>`. The outcome nodes are `<g onClick onMouseEnter>` elements — **not focusable, not operable by keyboard, with no text alternative**. This is the product's most important visual, and it is a picture of nothing to half the people who might use it.

**2. The table rows are click-only.**
`apps/studio/src/components/canvas/OpportunityLandscape.tsx:413-415` — `<tr onClick>` with no `tabIndex`, no `onKeyDown`, and no indication that the row is interactive.

**3. The job-map tiles are click-only.**
`apps/studio/src/components/canvas/JobMap.tsx:133-135` — `<div onClick>` with no `role="button"`, no `tabIndex`, no key handler.

**4. The notification cards are non-interactive elements that act like buttons.**
`apps/studio/src/components/notifications/CatchUpFeed.tsx:208-212` — `<article onClick={...}>`. The primary interaction of the catch-up feed is mouse-only, and assistive technology is not told it is actionable.

**5. The filter chips misuse the tab pattern.**
`apps/studio/src/components/notifications/CatchUpFeed.tsx:157-194` — `role="tablist"` / `role="tab"` with `aria-selected`, but **no `tabpanel`, no `aria-controls`, and no roving tabindex**. A screen reader announces tabs that control nothing, and the arrow-key behavior people expect from tabs does not exist.

**6. The unread count is never announced.**
`apps/studio/src/components/layout/StudioBar.tsx:60-73` — the badge is `aria-hidden="true"` and the bell's `aria-label` is the static string *"Catch up notifications"*. A screen-reader user never learns how many notifications are waiting.

**7. The search input has no label.**
`apps/studio/src/components/canvas/OpportunityLandscape.tsx:128-135` — placeholder only, no `<label>` and no `aria-label`.

**8. The whole transcript is one live region.**
`apps/studio/src/components/chat/Conversation.tsx:143` — the conversation is `aria-live="polite"`. Every streaming delta re-announces the whole region, so a long reply is read from the top, over and over.

**9. The command palette has no active-descendant.**
`apps/studio/src/components/chat/Composer.tsx:192-194` — the textarea carries `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, and `aria-autocomplete="list"`, but the highlighted option is never referenced with `aria-activedescendant`, so a keyboard user has no indication of the selection.

**10. Error toasts use the wrong role.**
`apps/studio/src/components/Toasts.tsx:11` — `role="status"` is used for errors; errors should be `role="alert"`.

**11. The mobile lens is a modal with no focus trap.**
`apps/studio/src/components/workspace/WorkspacePanel.tsx:44-49` — `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` with no focus trap and no escape handling. Compare `apps/studio/src/onboarding/FirstRunWizard.tsx:119-148`, which **does** implement a proper trap. The pattern exists in the codebase; it was not applied.

**12. Only one of the two lens layouts is ever tested.**
`apps/studio/src/lib/useMediaQuery.ts:27` — `useMediaQuery` returns `false` when `matchMedia` is missing, which is the case under jsdom. The mobile sheet path is what the tests exercise; the desktop dock path is untested.

**13. No automated check exists.**
There is no `axe-core` in the test suite, and no keyboard-traversal test. Every claim of accessibility in this repository is a claim, not a measurement.

**14. The one open PR that addresses this targets the wrong components.**
#66 adds a `MobileUX.test.tsx` that imports `ChatCopilot`, `StudioHeader`, and `CanvasTabs` — **none of which exist on `main`**. The components that actually ship — `StudioBar`, `ChatStage`, `WorkbenchRail`, `WorkspacePanel` — have no touch-target, focus-visible, or screen-reader treatment anywhere. Its `title=` tooltips (#63) are hover-only, which is the opposite of what touch needs.

## What a person experiences

A person who navigates by keyboard opens the Studio. The top bar's items are reachable with Tab and show a visible focus ring. They tab into the opportunity landscape and the matrix announces itself — *"Opportunity map, 12 outcomes, 4 underserved. Press Enter to open an outcome."* — and the outcome nodes are individually focusable. They open a notification card with Enter and it takes them to the outcome it names. A screen-reader user hears the unread count when it changes. The transcript announces **only the newest message** as it streams, not the entire history. Everything works with a keyboard, a screen reader, and a switch, because that is what accessible means.

## Specification

### 15.1 An automated gate

- Add `axe-core` and `vitest-axe` (or `@axe-core/playwright`) as dev dependencies in `apps/studio/package.json`.
- Add `apps/studio/src/test/a11y.test.tsx` — a test that renders each major surface and asserts **zero violations** of the axe rules at the WCAG 2.1 AA level:
  - `App` with the chat stage
  - the opportunity landscape (all three views: matrix, cards, table)
  - the job map
  - the catch-up feed
  - the settings panel
  - the first-run wizard
  - the command palette
- **The test must run in CI.** The `studio` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` already runs `npm test -- --run`; the axe tests are part of that suite and are **not** skipped in CI. Skipping them in CI is the usual failure mode and defeats the point.
- **Scope the rules deliberately.** `region` (all content in landmarks) and `color-contrast` are enabled. `color-contrast` needs a real rendering environment; if it cannot be tested reliably under jsdom, it must be tested in the Playwright pass (15.4) instead, and the axe test must scope it out **explicitly and visibly**, not silently.
- Every component must have a **stable accessible name**, so the tests are not brittle.

### 15.2 The matrix must be operable

`apps/studio/src/components/canvas/OpportunityLandscape.tsx:227-355`:

- The `<svg>` gets `role="img"`, a `<title>` ("Opportunity map"), and a `<desc>` summarizing it: *"N outcomes, M of them underserved, spanning importance X to Y."*
- **The SVG must not be the only representation.** Render a visually-hidden (`position: absolute; clip: rect(0 0 0 0)`) but accessible **list** of the same outcomes, or make the table view the accessible equivalent and link the two. The cleanest solution: the matrix gets `aria-hidden="true"` as a decorative duplicate of a real, accessible list that is always in the DOM.
- Each outcome node becomes a real focusable control: `tabIndex={0}`, `role="button"`, an `aria-label` naming the outcome and its score, `onKeyDown` handling Enter and Space, and a visible `:focus-visible` ring.
- The arrow keys move between nodes, so a keyboard user can traverse the map without tabbing through twelve stops. The roving tabindex pattern applies: one node is tabbable, the rest are reached with the arrow keys.
- `apps/studio/src/styles/theme.css` — add a `:focus-visible` treatment that is visible on every interactive surface, at a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against its background.

### 15.3 Every click-only surface becomes a real control

A **project-wide rule**: an element with an `onClick` is either a native control (`<button>`, `<a>`, `<input>`) or it has `role`, `tabIndex`, and an `onKeyDown`. Enforce it with a lint rule or a test that walks the rendered tree and flags click handlers on non-interactive elements.

Minimum list:

| Surface | File | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Landscape table rows | `OpportunityLandscape.tsx:413-415` | `tabIndex={0}` + `onKeyDown`, or make the first cell a real button |
| Job-map phase tiles | `JobMap.tsx:133-135` | `role="button"` + `tabIndex={0}` + `onKeyDown` |
| Notification cards | `CatchUpFeed.tsx:208-212` | `role="button"` + `tabIndex={0}` + `onKeyDown`; the "Ask Assistant" button inside must **stop propagation** so the card and the button do not both fire |
| Outcome nodes in the matrix | `OpportunityLandscape.tsx:227-355` | see 15.2 |
| `WorkbenchRail` items | `WorkbenchRail.tsx:26-60` | must be real buttons with `aria-current` for the active lens |
| `StudioBar` bell | `StudioBar.tsx:60-73` | a real button; the `aria-label` must include the unread count: *"Catch up notifications, 3 unread"* |
| `Toasts` dismiss | `Toasts.tsx` | a real button with an accessible name |

### 15.4 The ARIA that is wrong today

- **The filter chips** (`CatchUpFeed.tsx:157-194`) — replace the tablist with **buttons carrying `aria-pressed`**, and wrap the list in a region with an accessible name. If a tablist is wanted, it must have `tabpanel`s and a roving tabindex; the simpler and more honest option here is `aria-pressed`.
